testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-001
testCases.input: How many days of annual leave does a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service receive?
testCases.actualOutput: A full-time employee with less than 3 years’ service receives 27 days of annual leave, plus 8 bank holidays.
testCases.expectedOutput: A full-time employee with less than 3 years' continuous service receives 27 days of annual leave plus the 8 England and Wales bank holidays, a total of 35 paid days off per leave year (262.5 hours).
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.1 Entitlement **Table 3.1 — Annual leave entitlement (full-time, 37.5 hours over 5 days)** |**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave**
**days**|**Bank holidays**|**Total days**|**Total hours**| |---|---|---|---|---| |Less than 3 years|27|8|35|262.5| |3 years or more, less than 5 years|28|8|36|270.0| |5 years or more|29|8|37|277.5| Service increments apply from the first 1 January that falls after the employee completes the required service. ### **Service increment timing** - Start date 15 March 2024: 3 years completed on 14 March 2027. The first 1 January after that is 1 January 2028, so the employee receives 28 days from the 2028 leave year. In 2027 the entitlement remains 27 days. - Start date 1 January 2024: 3 years completed at the end of 31 December 2026. The first 1 January after that is 1 January 2027, so the employee receives 28 days in the 2027 leave year.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

Pro-rated entitlement = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / days in the leave year), rounded up (0.5 day for day-based, 0.25 hour for hours-based).

## **Worked examples 3.5 — joiners**

- **Full-time joiner, 1 March 2027:** 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.636, rounded up to **23.0 days** , plus 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027.

- **Full-time joiner, 16 September 2027:** calendar days 16 September to 31 December = 107. 27 x 107 / 365 = 7.915, rounded up to **8.0 days** , plus the 27 and 28 December bank holidays. Three of these days must be reserved for the 2027 shutdown (29 to 31 December).

- **Part-time joiner, 1 July 2027, 22.5 hours Monday to Wednesday:** 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397, rounded up to **79.5 hours** . Bank holidays on working days (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 22.5 hours. Bookable annual leave = **57.0 hours** .

## **Worked examples 3.5 — leavers**

- **Full-time leaver, 30 June 2027, salary £45,500:** 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Taken 10 days: balance 3.5 days x £175.00 = **£612.50** paid. Taken 15 days: balance −1.5 days x £175.00 = **£262.50** deducted where the contract permits.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

## **Worked example 3.4B — part-time to full-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday) from 1 January to 31 March 2027 (90 days), then full-time from 1 April to 31 December 2027 (275 days).

- Period 1: 157.5 x 90 / 365 = 38.836 hours

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

- **Part-time leaver, 31 March 2027, 30 hours Monday to Thursday, salary £32,000:** 210 x 90 / 365 = 51.781, rounded up to 52.0 hours. Bank holiday on a working day (29 March) = 7.5 hours, leaving 44.5 bookable hours. Taken 30 hours: balance 14.5 hours. Hourly rate = £32,000 / (52 x 30) = £20.5128. Payment = 14.5 x £20.5128 = **£297.44** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year)

- **Request submitted Thursday 1 October 2026** for 3 days starting Monday 12 October 2026. Working days between: 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 October = 6. The current rule (10 working days) applies, so this is **short notice** .

- **Part-time 2026 entitlement (3 days per week, 0.6 FTE, less than 5 years' service):** archived allowance 15 days (112.5 hours) plus bank holidays on working days, plus a transitional uplift of 3.75 x 0.6 = **2.25 hours** , giving 114.75 hours of annual leave.

testCases.input: What is the deadline for reporting sickness absence on the first day?
testCases.actualOutput: Report by 09:30 on the first day of absence. Shift and on-call workers must report at least 1 hour before their shift or rota period starts.
testCases.expectedOutput: Employees must call their line manager by telephone or Teams call no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least 1 hour before their shift or rota period starts. The absence must also be recorded in PeopleHub the same day.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.11 Sickness during annual leave

Report sickness by 09:30 on the first day of sickness under section 4.1, even while on leave. Provide self-certification (1 to 7 calendar days) or a fit note (more than 7 calendar days). The manager reclassifies the days in PeopleHub and the leave is re-credited. Sickness reported only after returning from leave is not normally reclassified.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.12 Sickness during annual leave

An employee who falls ill during annual leave may have the affected days reclassified as sickness absence and re-credited to their annual leave balance, provided that they:

1. report the sickness to their line manager by **09:30** on the first day of sickness (or as soon as reasonably practicable if they are in a different time zone), following section 7.1; and

2. provide self-certification for absences of up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note for absences of more than 7 calendar days, as set out in section 7.3.

Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence under section 7.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.2 Evidence

Self-certification covers up to 7 calendar days (including non-working days). A fit note is required for absences of more than 7 calendar days, submitted within 3 working days of issue. Northstar may require fit notes for all absences once an employee reaches Stage 1 of the attendance process and will reimburse any charge.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-003
testCases.input: What is the deadline for submitting an expense claim?
testCases.actualOutput: Submit your expense claim within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred.
testCases.expectedOutput: Expense claims must be submitted in ExpenseFlow within 30 calendar days of the date the expense was incurred. Claims 31 to 90 days late need a written explanation and Head of Department approval; claims more than 90 days late are not reimbursed without a Finance Director exception.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Submission deadlines

### **Deadlines**

- Submit within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. For multi-day trips, each expense's own date applies, but all expenses for one trip should be submitted together within 30 calendar days of the first expense of the trip.

- **31 to 90 calendar days:** a late claim requires a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- **More than 90 calendar days:** not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the claimant was on long-term sickness or family leave).

- **Leavers:** all claims must be submitted within **10 working days** after the leaving date. Claims received after that are not paid.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

- A claim fully approved on 9 March 2027 is paid on Thursday 25 March 2027. A claim fully approved on 12 March 2027 is paid in the April payroll; because 25 April 2027 is a Sunday, it is paid on Friday 23 April 2027.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Reimbursement timelines

Expenses are reimbursed through payroll. Claims that are fully approved by the payroll cut-off (the **10th of the month** ) are paid on the 25th of the same month (or the previous working day if the 25th is not a working day). Claims fully approved after the 10th are paid in the following month's payroll. Finance may make an off-cycle payment for approved claims over £500 where waiting would cause hardship.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.4 — crossing the 10,000-mile threshold**

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

# **Example 14.7 — late claims and reimbursement dates**

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-008
testCases.input: On what day of the month is salary paid?
testCases.actualOutput: Salary is paid on the 25th of each month. If it falls on a weekend or bank holiday, it is paid on the previous working day.
testCases.expectedOutput: Salaries are paid monthly, for the calendar month, by bank transfer on the 25th of each month. If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, salary is paid on the previous working day.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.1 Salary payment

Salaries are paid monthly, for the calendar month, by bank transfer on the **25th of each month** . If the 25th falls on a weekend or bank holiday, salary is paid on the previous working day.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.11 Final pay and outstanding annual leave

Salary is paid for the calendar month on the 25th (section 11.1). If the leaving date is **on or before** the 10th of a month, all final pay, including payment for untaken annual leave, approved expenses and any deductions, is paid on the 25th of that month. If the leaving date is **after** the 10th, normal salary for that month is paid on the 25th and the final adjustments (holiday pay, expenses and deductions) are paid on the 25th of the following month. The final holiday balance is calculated as set out in section 6.17.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.2 Payroll cut-off

The payroll cut-off is the **10th of each month** . Changes received and approved by the cut-off (new starters, leavers, bank-detail changes, overtime, approved expenses, allowances and unpaid leave) are processed in that month's payroll. Items received after the cut-off are processed in the following month's payroll. A new starter whose details are incomplete at the cut-off is paid in the next payroll; on request, People Operations may arrange an advance of net pay.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.3 Payslips

Payslips are published in PeopleHub by the **23rd of each month** . Each payslip shows gross pay, deductions and net pay, as required by law.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.6 Salary reviews

Salaries are reviewed annually, with any change normally effective from **1 April** . Salary review increases are discretionary and are not guaranteed, except where a contract or collective agreement provides otherwise or where an increase is needed to meet the National Minimum Wage.

testCases.input: How quickly must I report a lost or stolen company laptop?
testCases.actualOutput: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately, and no later than 1 hour after discovering it. If it was stolen, report the theft to police within 24 hours and add the crime reference number to your IT ticket.
testCases.expectedOutput: Report loss or theft of any device to the IT Service Desk immediately and in any case within 1 hour of discovery so it can be locked and wiped remotely. Theft must also be reported to the police within 24 hours, with the crime reference recorded in the IT ticket. Loss or theft is also a security incident.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.3 Damage, loss and theft

- Report loss or theft of any device or access card to the IT Service Desk **immediately and in any case within 1 hour** of discovery, so that it can be locked and wiped remotely. Loss or theft is also a security incident (section 19.10).

- Report theft to the police within **24 hours** and record the crime reference number in the IT ticket.

- Report accidental damage to the IT Service Desk as soon as possible. Northstar does not normally recover the cost of accidental damage. Where loss or damage results from deliberate misuse or gross negligence, Northstar may recover a reasonable contribution only with the employee's written agreement or where the contract permits.

19 IT acceptable use, information security and AI usage > 19.10 Security incident reporting

All suspected security incidents — including lost or stolen devices, malware, phishing that resulted in a click or credential entry, unauthorised access, and suspected prompt-injection or misuse of AI tools — must be reported to the IT Service Desk (ithelp@northstar.example) or security@northstar.example **within 1 hour** of discovery. Severity 1 incidents (for example, suspected compromise of Restricted information) must be reported immediately by phone to the 24/7 security line. Detailed severity levels are in NDS-SEC-ITG-004 section 9.

20 Company equipment and property > 20.6 Returning equipment

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

- **Remote or hybrid leavers** return all equipment within **5 working days** after their leaving date, using the prepaid courier arranged by IT. Access cards may be posted with the equipment.

- If equipment has not been returned within **10 working days** after the leaving date, IT escalates to People Operations, who send a written reminder and may take recovery action. Any deduction from final pay is made only where the contract permits or the employee has agreed in writing.

- Employees returning from long-term absence or moving role return any equipment no longer needed within 10 working days of IT's request.

retrievalContext:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.1 Eligibility

Every employee may make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and may make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . Contractors and agency workers cannot use this procedure.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.6 Formal flexible-working requests

All employees can make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and can make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . A request can cover hours, start and finish times, working days, or place of work.

## **Flexible working — process and deadlines**

1. Submit a written request in PeopleHub stating that it is a statutory request for flexible working, the date of the request, the working pattern requested and the proposed start date, and whether and when any earlier request was made. 2. The line manager acknowledges the request within **5 working days** . 3. The line manager meets the employee to discuss the request within **4 weeks** of receiving it. A request cannot be refused without first consulting the employee. 4. A written decision is issued, and any appeal concluded, within **2 months** of the date of the request, unless the employee agrees to an extension. 5. A refusal must give one or more of the statutory business reasons and explain why it applies. 6. The employee may appeal within **10 working days** of the decision. The appeal is heard by a different, more senior manager.

The statutory business reasons for refusing a request are: the burden of additional costs; inability to reorganise work among existing staff; inability to recruit additional staff; a detrimental effect on quality; a detrimental effect on performance; a detrimental effect on ability to meet customer demand; insufficient work during the periods the employee proposes to work; and planned structural changes. Managers may agree a **trial period of up to 3 months** before confirming a permanent change.

Managers may agree a trial of up to **3 months** , recorded with a review date. At the end of the trial, the arrangement becomes permanent, is extended once by up to 3 months, or ends with reasons given. A permanent change is a contractual variation confirmed in writing by People Operations within 14 days.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-015
testCases.input: What's the cut-off for letting my boss know I'm off sick?
testCases.actualOutput: Call your line manager by 09:30 on your first day off sick. If you work shifts or are on call, call at least 1 hour before your shift or rota period starts.
testCases.expectedOutput: You must call (phone or Teams call) your line manager no later than 09:30 on your first day of sickness; messages alone are not enough unless you physically cannot speak. Record the absence in PeopleHub the same day.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 4 Sickness absence > 4.1 Reporting **Table 4.1 — Sickness reporting requirements** |**Requirement**|**Rule**| |---|---| |Deadline|By**09:30**on the first day of absence; shift and on-call workers at least 1 hour before
the shift or rota period.| |Channel|Telephone or Teams call to the line manager (Head of Department or team lead if
unavailable). Text, chat or email alone is not sufficient unless the employee is
physically unable to speak.| |Record|Absence recorded in PeopleHub the same day by the employee or manager.| |Updates|On the third working day, then at least weekly.| |Return|Self-certification on return; return-to-work conversation within 2 working days.|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.7 Return to work and phased return

Return-to-work conversations take place within 2 working days of return. Phased returns of up to 4 weeks are on full pay; longer phased returns need Head of Department approval, with the balance of hours covered by annual leave or remaining company sick pay.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.2 Keeping in touch during absence

Employees must update their line manager on the **third working day** of absence and then at least **weekly** , unless a different arrangement is agreed. The line manager is responsible for maintaining supportive, proportionate contact; for long-term absence, contact should be at least every 2 weeks and agreed with the employee.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.11 Sickness during annual leave

Report sickness by 09:30 on the first day of sickness under section 4.1, even while on leave. Provide self-certification (1 to 7 calendar days) or a fit note (more than 7 calendar days). The manager reclassifies the days in PeopleHub and the leave is re-credited. Sickness reported only after returning from leave is not normally reclassified.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-016
testCases.input: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
testCases.actualOutput:
Yes. You can normally carry over up to 5 days of unused holiday, and must use them by 31 March of the next leave year.

Exceptions may allow more: sickness absence can qualify for up to 4 additional weeks; family-related leave can allow all untaken leave for the year; and exceptional business reasons can allow 5 extra days with approval and a request by 30 November.
testCases.expectedOutput: Up to 5 days of unused annual leave (37.5 hours full-time; pro-rated by FTE for part-time) can be carried into the next leave year without approval, and must be taken by 31 March. Further carryover is available only for sickness, family-related leave, or exceptional business reasons approved by the Director of People Operations.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.11 Carrying over unused leave ## **Standard carryover rule** Up to **5 days** (37.5 hours for a full-time employee; pro-rated for part-time employees by FTE) of unused annual leave may be carried over into the next leave year without approval. Carried-over leave must be taken by **31 March** of the next leave year. Carried-over leave not taken by 31 March is lost, unless one of the exceptions below applies. **Table 6.11 — Carryover exceptions** |**Situation**|**Rule**|**Approval and deadline**| |---|---|---| |Employee could not take leave

Operations. Must be taken by 30 June of

return-to-work date|Automatic| |Exceptional business reasons|A further 5 days (10 days

November| ## **Worked examples 3.8 — carryover** - **Standard:** a full-time employee has 27 days in 2027 and has taken 20 days by 31 December 2027 (including the 3 shutdown days). Unused = 7 days. They carry over **5 days** , which must be taken by 31 March 2028, and **2 days are lost** unless an exception is approved. - **Part-time limit:** an employee at 0.6 FTE may carry over up to 37.5 x 0.6 = **22.5 hours** . - **Sickness:** a full-time employee was on sick leave from September to December 2027 and has 15 unused days. They carry over 5 standard days (use by 31 March 2028) and the remaining 10 days under the sickness rule (use by 30 June 2029, 18 months after 31 December 2027). - **2026 into 2027:** a full-time employee with a 2026 transitional entitlement of 25.5 days took 22 days in 2026. Unused = 3.5 days, which is within the 5-day limit, so all **3.5 days** carry over and must be taken by 31 March 2027.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.15 Transitional arrangements for the 2026 leave year Version 2.0 of this handbook and the Leave and Absence Standard NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2 replaced the archived Leave Policy NDS-HR-LV-006 v1.0 on **1 October 2026** . The following transitional rules apply: **Table 6.15 — Transitional rules, 2026 leave year** |**Topic**|**Transitional rule**| |---|---| |2026 annual leave entitlement (full-time, less
than 5 years' service)|**25.5 days**plus bank holidays: 25 days under the archived policy plus an uplift of 0.5
day (the 2-day increase x 3/12, for October to December 2026).| |2026 entitlement, part-time|The archived-policy allowance plus an uplift of 3.75 hours x FTE.| |2026 service increments|Increments awarded under the archived policy (1 extra day after 5 years) continue
for 2026. The new increments in Table 6.1 apply from 1 January 2027.| |Notice for requests|Requests submitted before 1 October 2026 are assessed against the notice rules in

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year) **Table 3.9 — Transitional rules from the archived Leave Policy NDS-HR-LV-006 v1.0** |**Topic**|**Archived policy v1.0 (1 Jan 2025 – 30 Sep**
**2026)**|**This Standard v1.2 (from 1 Oct 2026)**| |---|---|---| |Full-time annual leave|25 days plus bank holidays|27 days plus bank holidays (2027
onwards)| |2026 full-time entitlement|—|25.5 days (less than 5 years' service); 26.5
days (5 years or more)| |Service increments|+1 day after 5 years|+1 day after 3 years; +2 days after 5 years
(from 1 January 2027)| |Notice for up to 5 days|5 working days|2 working days (up to 1 day); 10 working
days (more than 1 and up to 5 days)| |Notice for more than 5 days|20 working days|20 working days (up to 10 days); 40
working days (more than 10 days)| |Manager response time|10 working days|5 working days| |Carryover|3 days, use by 28 February|5 days, use by 31 March| |Hourly leave|Not available|Available from 1 October 2026| |Negative balance|Not permitted|Up to 3 days with Head of Department
approval| |Sickness reporting deadline|10:00|09:30| **Which rules apply to a request?** The notice and approval rules are those in force on the date the request was submitted. Entitlement and carryover are determined by the leave year. ### **Worked examples 3.9 — transition** - **Request submitted Monday 28 September 2026** for 3 days starting Tuesday 6 October 2026. Working days between: 29 and 30 September, 1, 2 and 5 October = 5. The request was submitted before 1 October 2026, so the archived rule (5 working days for up to 5 days) applies and the notice requirement is **met** .

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-017
testCases.input: Do I need a doctor's note if I'm off ill for three days?
testCases.actualOutput: No. For three calendar days off sick, self-certification is enough; complete the form in PeopleHub on the day you return.
testCases.expectedOutput: For absences of 1 to 7 calendar days (including non-working days) you complete a self-certification form in PeopleHub on your return. A fit note is required only for absences of more than 7 calendar days, unless you are at Stage 1 or above of the attendance process, when Northstar may ask for one and reimburse the cost.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.2 Evidence

Self-certification covers up to 7 calendar days (including non-working days). A fit note is required for absences of more than 7 calendar days, submitted within 3 working days of issue. Northstar may require fit notes for all absences once an employee reaches Stage 1 of the attendance process and will reimburse any charge.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.3 Self-certification and medical evidence **Table 7.3 — Evidence required for sickness absence** |**Length of absence (calendar days,**
**including non-working days)**|**Evidence required**| |---|---| |1 to 7 calendar days|Self-certification form in PeopleHub, completed on the day of return.| |More than 7 calendar days|A fit note from a doctor or another healthcare professional who is permitted to issue
fit notes, covering the period from day 8 onwards, submitted within 3 working days of
being issued. Further fit notes must be provided before the previous one expires.| |Repeated short-term absence (Stage 1 or
above under section 7.6)|Northstar may request a fit note for any further absence. Northstar will reimburse any
charge for obtaining it.| ## **Fit notes** Employees must give their employer a fit note if they are off work for more than 7 days in a row, including non-working days. A fit note may state that the employee is "not fit for work" or "may be fit for work" with adjustments such as a phased return, altered hours, amended duties or workplace adaptations. Where a fit note says "may be fit for work", the line manager discusses whether the suggested adjustments can be accommodated.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.11 Sickness during annual leave

Report sickness by 09:30 on the first day of sickness under section 4.1, even while on leave. Provide self-certification (1 to 7 calendar days) or a fit note (more than 7 calendar days). The manager reclassifies the days in PeopleHub and the leave is re-credited. Sickness reported only after returning from leave is not normally reclassified.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.6 Long-term absence and Occupational Health

Absence of 4 consecutive weeks or more is long-term; an Occupational Health referral is normally made at that point. Welfare contact is agreed with the employee and takes place at least every 2 weeks.

testCases.input: Is there any money towards setting up my desk at home?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes. If you work hybrid or remotely and have completed probation, you can claim up to £300 including VAT for a desk, chair or other ergonomic equipment, once in any 3-year period. Submit the claim through ExpenseFlow with receipts.
testCases.expectedOutput: Hybrid and remote employees who have completed probation may claim a home office allowance of up to £300 (including VAT) once in any 3-year period for a desk, chair or other ergonomic equipment, with receipts, through ExpenseFlow. Equipment provided as a reasonable adjustment is funded separately.

10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.4 Home-working equipment

Northstar provides a laptop, one external monitor, a keyboard, a mouse and a headset to hybrid and remote employees. After completing probation, employees may claim a **home office allowance of up to £300** (including VAT), once in any 3-year period, for a desk, chair or other ergonomic equipment, with receipts, through ExpenseFlow. Equipment provided as a reasonable adjustment is funded separately and does not count towards the allowance.

Working from home

Working from abroad isn't available during probation. After that it's limited to 10 working days in a rolling 12 months.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-019
testCases.input: Can I use free AI chatbots for my work?
testCases.actualOutput: Only with public information; free or consumer AI chatbots must not receive Northstar Internal, Confidential, personal or Restricted information. Use Northstar Assist for permitted Northstar work information, and never enter Restricted information in any AI tool.
testCases.expectedOutput: Public or consumer AI services may be used with Public information only. You must never sign in with Northstar credentials or upload Northstar files, and entering Internal, Confidential or personal data into them is prohibited. For Internal or Confidential Northstar information, use an approved service such as Northstar Assist, and never enter Restricted information into any AI tool.

## Classification decides which tool you can use

|Classification|Examples|Approved enterprise AI tool|Public or consumer AI tool|

|Public|Website content, job adverts|Yes|Yes|

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-020
testCases.input: My kid's nursery shut out of the blue today — what time off can I take?
testCases.actualOutput:
You can take reasonable time off for this unexpected emergency involving your child. Northstar pays up to 2 working days for the occurrence, subject to a maximum of 5 paid days in the leave year; after that, the time is unpaid unless you choose annual leave.
Notify your line manager by phone as soon as reasonably practicable.
testCases.expectedOutput: This is an emergency involving a dependant, covered by the statutory right to a reasonable amount of time off for dependants (unpaid by law, from day one). Northstar pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, up to 5 paid days per leave year; further time is unpaid or you may use annual leave. Call your line manager as soon as possible.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.10 Company shutdown

Three days are reserved each year for the shutdown between Christmas and New Year: 29 to 31 December 2026 and 29 to 31 December 2027. Part-time employees reserve only the shutdown days that fall on their working days. Employees rostered to work during the shutdown take the equivalent leave at another time agreed with their manager.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.14 Company shutdown Northstar closes its offices for 3 working days between Christmas and New Year. Employees must reserve **3 days** of annual leave for the shutdown (or the shutdown days that fall on their working days, for part-time employees). Shutdown dates are published by **31 January** each year. **Table 6.14 — Company shutdown dates** |**Leave year**|**Shutdown dates**|**Days to reserve (full-time)**| |---|---|---| |2026|Tuesday 29, Wednesday 30 and Thursday 31
December 2026|3 days| |2027|Wednesday 29, Thursday 30 and Friday 31
December 2027|3 days| Employees on the customer support or on-call rota during the shutdown work as rostered and take the equivalent leave at another time. New starters with insufficient leave may take unpaid leave for the shutdown or, with manager agreement, work remotely.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Card 5.5 — Unpaid parental leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Employees from day one (since 6 April 2026) named on the birth or adoption certificate or with
parental responsibility, for a child under 18.| |Entitlement and pay|18 weeks per child; maximum 4 weeks per child per year; whole weeks unless the child is disabled
or Northstar agrees otherwise. Unpaid.| |Notice|21 days before the start date, stating start and end dates.| |Approver and deadline|Line manager responds within 7 days; postponement of up to 6 months only for undue business
disruption, confirmed in writing within 7 days with new dates (not available for leave immediately
after a birth or adoption).| |Escalation and records|Head of Department; PeopleHub records the weeks used per child.| # **Worked example 5.5 — parental leave balance** An employee has two children and took 3 weeks of parental leave for their elder child in 2027. In 2027 they may take at most 1 more week for the elder child (4-week annual limit per child) and up to 4 weeks for the younger child. The elder child's lifetime balance is 18 − 3 = 15 weeks remaining. **Card 5.6 — Neonatal care leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Eligibility|Leave: employees from day one whose baby was admitted to neonatal care within 28 days of birth
for at least 7 full consecutive days. Statutory pay: 26 weeks' continuous service and minimum
earnings. Company top-up: 26 weeks' continuous service.| |Entitlement and pay|One week per full week in neonatal care, up to 12 weeks, taken within 68 weeks of birth. Full basic
pay with 26 weeks' service; otherwise statutory pay if eligible, or unpaid.| |Notice and approver|Notify the line manager as soon as possible; People Operations confirms. No approval required.|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 5 Family-related leave procedures ## **Card 5.7 — Time off for dependants and carer's leave** |**Element**|**Detail**| |---|---| |Time off for dependants|Reasonable unpaid time for unexpected emergencies involving a dependant (statutory, day one).
Company pays up to 2 working days per occurrence, maximum 5 paid days per leave year. Notify

dependant with a long-term care need. Notice: at least 3 days for up to 1 day; at least twice the
length of leave for more than 1 day. No evidence required. Company pays the first 3 days in any
rolling 12 months.| |Approver and escalation|Line manager; Head of Department. Carer's leave may be postponed only where operations would
be unduly disrupted, with an alternative date within 1 month.| # **Worked examples 5.7 — dependants and carer's leave** - An employee's childminder cancels unexpectedly on Monday and they take Monday and Tuesday off to arrange care: 2 paid days (time off for dependants). Later in the same leave year they have used 5 paid days in total; a further emergency day is unpaid unless they choose annual leave. - An employee requests 2 days of carer's leave starting Monday 8 March 2027. Notice must be at least 4 days (twice the leave). A request made on Wednesday 3 March 2027 gives 5 days' notice and is valid. The first 3 carer's leave days in the rolling 12 months are paid, so both days are paid if no carer's leave was taken in the previous 12 months.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.6 Neonatal care leave and pay

Parents whose baby is admitted to neonatal care within 28 days of birth and stays in care for at least 7 full, consecutive days can take up to **12 weeks** of neonatal care leave (one week for each full week the baby spends in neonatal care). Leave is a day-one right and must be taken within 68 weeks of the birth. Statutory Neonatal Care Pay requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service and minimum earnings. Northstar tops up Statutory Neonatal Care Pay to **full basic pay** for employees with at least 26 weeks' continuous service. Neonatal care leave is taken in addition to other family leave.

testCases.actualOutput: For business miles in your own car, you get 55p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year, then 25p per mile after that. Only business miles count; deduct your normal commute distance if the trip starts or ends at home.
testCases.expectedOutput: Car mileage is reimbursed at 55p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and 25p per mile thereafter (HMRC approved rates). Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.1 — two-day London trip**

A Manchester-based consultant travels to London on Tuesday and returns Wednesday, with an approved overnight stay.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

testCases.input: My manager hasn't answered my holiday request — does that mean it's OK?
testCases.actualOutput: No. A holiday request is not approved by default if your manager hasn’t responded; it must show as “Approved” in PeopleHub before you take the leave. If there’s no decision within 5 working days of submission, PeopleHub automatically escalates it to the Head of Department.
testCases.expectedOutput: Managers must decide within 5 working days. If there is no decision, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because the manager did not respond, and you should not book non-refundable travel until it shows as Approved.

6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.9 Declined requests and escalation

A manager who declines a request must record the business reason in PeopleHub. The employee may ask the Head of Department to review the decision within **5 working days** of the decline. The Head of Department will respond within **5 working days** of receiving the review request, and their decision is final under this policy. This does not affect the employee's right to raise a grievance under section 15.6.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.8 Overlapping requests from colleagues

Where requests from colleagues would exceed the team coverage limit, the request submitted first in PeopleHub normally has priority. For high-demand periods (the 2 weeks around Christmas and New Year, and school summer holidays), managers may instead use a fair rotation based on who had leave in the same period in the previous year, provided this is explained to the team in advance. Managers must not decide between overlapping requests on the basis of a protected characteristic, and should consider requests linked to religious observance or caring responsibilities sympathetically.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)

- Unless the Head of Department approves otherwise, no more than **30% of a team** (rounded down, with a minimum of one person) may be on planned annual leave on the same working day. For a team of 8 this is 2 people; for a team of 3 it is 1 person.

- A Head of Department may designate a **critical delivery period** (for example, a customer go-live, a data-centre migration or the Finance year-end close) by publishing it in PeopleHub at least **6 weeks** before it starts. A critical delivery period may last no more than **15 working days** , and no team may have more than **2** critical delivery periods in a leave year.

- Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-023
testCases.input: Can I take a couple of hours off instead of a whole day?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes. You can take annual leave in whole-hour blocks, with a minimum of 1 hour; up to 37.5 hours per leave year can be taken this way, pro-rated for part-time employees.
testCases.expectedOutput: Hourly leave may be taken in whole-hour blocks with a minimum of 1 hour. Up to 37.5 hours of annual leave per leave year may be taken as hourly leave (pro-rated for part-time employees). It needs at least 2 working days' notice like other leave of up to 1 day.
retrievalContext:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Office attendance standard > 4.3 Part-time employees and absence

The requirement is pro-rated and rounded **up** to the nearest whole day:

- **Part-time:** required days = 8 x (contracted working days per week / 5). For a 3-day week: 8 x 3 / 5 = 4.8, rounded up to **5 days** per rolling 4-week period.

- **Annual leave, sickness, bank holidays and other approved absence:** required days = (normal requirement) x (available working days in the period / normal working days in the period). For a full-time employee with 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period of 20 working days: 8 x 15 / 20 = **6 days** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-024
testCases.input: Who can I go to if I think someone is fiddling the books, and can I stay anonymous?
testCases.actualOutput: You can report suspected misconduct to your line manager or People Operations, or use the whistleblowing channels, including speakup@northstar.example or the independent Speak Up line. The Speak Up line accepts anonymous reports; if you ask for your identity to be protected, Northstar will do so unless disclosure is required by law.
testCases.expectedOutput: Suspected fraud is a whistleblowing matter. You can raise it with your line manager or Head of Department, the Head of Risk and Compliance (compliance@northstar.example), speakup@northstar.example, or the independent 24/7 Speak Up line, which accepts anonymous reports. Concerns involving your own management line should go outside it. Whistleblowers are protected from retaliation.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
16 Whistleblowing and reporting concerns > 16.5 Confidentiality and protection from retaliation

Northstar will protect the identity of a person raising a concern where they ask for this, unless disclosure is required by law. Anyone who victimises or retaliates against a whistleblower will face disciplinary action. Deliberately making a false report is a disciplinary matter.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
16 Whistleblowing and reporting concerns > 16.6 Urgent matters

If there is an immediate risk to life or health, call emergency services on 999 first, then Northstar Security. Suspected personal-data breaches must also be reported immediately to the Data Protection Officer (section 18.7); suspected security incidents to the IT Security team (section 19.10).

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 12 Fraud indicators and investigations **Table 12.1 — Common expense fraud indicators** |**Indicator**|**Example**| |---|---| |Altered or duplicated receipts|A receipt edited to show a higher amount, or the same receipt submitted twice in
different months.| |Split claims|A £400 hotel stay submitted as two £200 claims to avoid Head of Department
approval.| |Personal items claimed as business|Family meals claimed as client entertainment.| |Inflated mileage|Mileage that exceeds the route distance or includes commuting miles.| |Claims during leave|Expenses dated on days the claimant was on annual leave.| |Round-number or missing-receipt patterns|Frequent missing-receipt declarations just under the £75 limit.| Suspected fraud is investigated by Finance and People Operations under the disciplinary procedure. Expense fraud is normally gross misconduct. Northstar will recover any overpayment and may report suspected criminal offences to the police.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Standards of conduct and conflicts of interest > 14.11 Reporting suspected misconduct

Employees should report suspected misconduct to their line manager, People Operations or, where appropriate, through the whistleblowing procedure in section 16. Reports are handled confidentially as far as possible.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-025
testCases.input: I'm in month 4 of my probation and was off sick for 4 days. Will I get company sick pay?
testCases.actualOutput: No. During probation, the sick-pay entitlement is SSP only, not company sick pay. SSP is payable from the first qualifying day if you meet the statutory conditions.
testCases.expectedOutput: Company sick pay depends on service: during probation the entitlement is SSP only. Since 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness at the lower of £123.25 a week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, provided statutory conditions are met. You must have followed the reporting and self-certification rules.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.4 Company sick pay

**Table 4.4 — Company sick pay (inclusive of SSP) in any rolling 12 months**

|**Continuous service on first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed, less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more, less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

Your first six months at Northstar: New Starter Induction (NDS-HR-PRES-012 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 5

## If you're ill

Call by 09:30
Phone or Teams call to your manager on day one. A message alone isn't enough.
Log it
Record the absence in PeopleHub the same day.
Keep in touch
Update your manager on day 3, then weekly.
Evidence
Self-certify up to 7 calendar days; a fit note after that.
During probation you receive Statutory Sick Pay from day one (£123.25 a week or 80% of earnings, whichever is lower). Company sick pay starts once probation is passed.

Speaker notes: Shift workers and on-call staff call at least 1 hour before their shift. After probation, company sick pay is 4 weeks full pay then 4 weeks half pay in any rolling 12 months for employees with less than 2 years' service.

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 6

## Sickness: call by 09:30, SSP from day one

Employees call (phone or Teams) by 09:30 on day one; messages alone are not enough
Self-certify up to 7 calendar days; fit note after that
Since 6 April 2026, SSP is paid from the first day: £123.25 a week or 80% of earnings, whichever is lower
Company sick pay is inclusive of SSP and starts after probation
Pregnancy-related absence never counts towards triggers

Speaker notes: Company sick pay in any rolling 12 months: during probation SSP only; probation completed and under 2 years, 4 weeks full pay then 4 weeks half pay; 2 to under 5 years, 8 weeks full then 8 weeks half; 5 years or more, 13 weeks full then 13 weeks half. Attendance triggers: 3 separate absences or 8 working days in a rolling 12 months starts a supportive Stage 0 review. Disability-related absence is recorded separately and triggers may be adjusted.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.3 Statutory Sick Pay

From 6 April 2026, SSP is payable from the first qualifying day of sickness at the lower of £123.25 per week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days are contracted working days. The daily SSP rate is the weekly rate divided by the number of qualifying days in the week.

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-027
testCases.input: I joined Northstar 2 months before my partner's due date. Can I take paternity leave, and will it be paid?
testCases.actualOutput: You can take up to 2 weeks of paternity leave if you are your partner’s partner and expect to have responsibility for the child’s upbringing. Because you joined only 2 months before the due date, you won’t have the required 26 weeks’ service by the qualifying week, so the leave will be unpaid; you may choose to use annual leave instead.
testCases.expectedOutput: Paternity leave is a day-one right since 6 April 2026, so you may take up to 2 weeks (one block or two 1-week blocks, ending within 52 weeks of the birth), provided you give notice of the due date at least 15 weeks before it (or as soon as reasonably practicable given your start date — confirm with People Operations). Statutory Paternity Pay and Northstar's full-pay enhancement both require 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth, so with about 2 months' service you are not eligible; the leave is unpaid, but you may use annual leave instead.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.2 Paternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Since 6 April 2026, paternity leave is a day-one right for eligible employees. An employee who is the biological father of the child, or the partner of the mother or adopter, and who expects to have responsibility for the child's upbringing, may take up to **2 weeks** of paternity leave, as one 2-week block or two separate 1-week blocks. Leave cannot start before the birth and must end within 52 weeks of the birth (or of the due date if the baby is born early).

**Notice.** The employee must tell People Operations the due date at least 15 weeks before the baby is due, and must give 28 days' notice to change the start date of paternity leave.

**Statutory Paternity Pay.** SPP is £194.32 per week or 90% of AWE, whichever is lower. It requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the EWC), continued employment up to the date of birth, and AWE of at least £129.

**Northstar enhancement.** Employees who qualify for SPP receive **full basic pay for 2 weeks** , inclusive of SPP. Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid; they may choose to use annual leave instead for some or all of the period.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.5 Unpaid parental leave

Since 6 April 2026, unpaid parental leave is a day-one right for eligible employees. Employees with parental responsibility may take up to **18 weeks** of unpaid parental leave for each child up to the child's 18th birthday, with a maximum of **4 weeks per child in any year** . Leave must be taken in whole weeks unless the child is disabled or Northstar agrees otherwise, and the employee must give **21 days' notice** of the start and end dates. Northstar may postpone leave for up to 6 months where the business would be unduly disrupted, except where leave is requested to start immediately after a birth or adoption; any postponement is confirmed in writing within 7 days of the request with the new dates. Northstar may ask for reasonable proof of parental responsibility but will not ask for it each time leave is requested.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.7 Pregnancy and adoption appointments

- Pregnant employees have a statutory right to reasonable **paid** time off for antenatal care, including relaxation and parenting classes recommended by a doctor or midwife. After the first appointment, Northstar may ask to see an appointment card and confirmation of pregnancy.

- Partners of a pregnant woman have a statutory right to unpaid time off to accompany her to up to two antenatal appointments, of up to 6.5 hours each. Northstar pays this time in full as a company enhancement.

- Employees adopting a child can take time off for adoption appointments in line with the statutory scheme; Northstar pays this time in full.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.1 Maternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Pregnant employees are entitled to up to 52 weeks of Statutory Maternity Leave (26 weeks of Ordinary Maternity Leave and 26 weeks of Additional Maternity Leave), regardless of length of service, hours or pay. The earliest leave can start is 11 weeks before the EWC. Employees must take at least 2 weeks of compulsory maternity leave after the birth.

**Notice.** By the end of the 15th week before the EWC, the employee must tell People Operations (via PeopleHub) that she is pregnant, her EWC and the date she wants maternity leave to start. Northstar will confirm the expected return date in writing within 28 days. To change the return date, the employee must give at least 8 weeks' notice.

**Statutory Maternity Pay.** SMP requires at least 28 days' notice of the date SMP should start and evidence of pregnancy (a MATB1 certificate or a letter from a doctor or midwife) within 21 days of the SMP start date. A MATB1 cannot be issued more than 20 weeks before the due date. Employees who do not qualify for SMP may be able to claim Maternity Allowance from the government; Northstar will issue form SMP1 explaining why SMP is not payable.

**Northstar enhanced maternity pay.** Employees who qualify for SMP **and** have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive:

**Table 8.1 — Northstar enhanced maternity and adoption pay**

|**Weeks of leave**|**Payment**|
|---|---|
|Weeks 1 to 16|Full basic pay, inclusive of SMP or SAP.|
|Weeks 17 to 39|SMP or SAP only.|
|Weeks 40 to 52|Unpaid.|

If the employee does not return to work for at least **6 months** after the end of maternity leave, she must repay the enhanced element (the amount paid above SMP), unless employment ends because of redundancy, ill-health capability, or a further period of statutory family leave immediately following the first. Statutory pay is never repayable because an employee does not return.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.4 Shared parental leave and pay

Eligible parents can share up to **50 weeks** of leave and up to **37 weeks** of pay by ending maternity or adoption leave early. Eligibility depends on both parents: the employee must meet the continuity of employment test (normally 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or by the week of matching, and still employed in the first week of shared parental leave), and the other parent must meet the employment and earnings test. The employee must give at least **8 weeks' written notice** of leave dates. Requests for discontinuous blocks may be refused; the employee may then take the leave as one continuous block. Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.

7 Working from outside the UK > 7.3 Worked examples

## **Work From Abroad examples**

- **Within the limit:** An employee who has not worked abroad in the past 12 months requests to work from Portugal for 5 working days in July 2027, submitting the request 6 weeks ahead. Approvable, subject to all three approvals.

- **Rolling limit exceeded:** An employee worked abroad for 6 days in February 2027 and asks for 5 days in October 2027. Within the rolling 12 months this would total 11 days, so only **4 days** can be approved unless the Director of People Operations approves an exception (maximum 20 days).

- **Restricted customer data:** An employee who supports a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data) asks to work from Italy for a week. They may work abroad only on tasks that do not involve Restricted data, unless the CISO approves in writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK. The manager arranges UK-based cover for Restricted tasks.

- **Short notice:** A request submitted 10 days before travel does not meet the 4-week notice requirement and will normally be declined.

- **Probation:** An employee in month 4 of probation asks to work from Spain for 3 days. Not eligible until probation is completed.

- **Holiday email:** An employee on annual leave in France briefly reads email on their phone. This is not a working day abroad. Joining a customer call or accessing customer systems would be, and requires approval.

10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.8 Working overseas and cross-border working

Working from outside the UK raises tax, social security, immigration, insurance, employment-law and data-protection risks for both the employee and Northstar.

- Employees who have completed probation and are not serving notice may work temporarily from another country for up to **10 working days** in any rolling 12-month period, only with prior approval through the "Work From Abroad" request in PeopleHub, submitted at least **4 weeks** before travel and approved by the line manager, People Operations and IT Security.

- Work from abroad is not permitted from countries on the IT Security restricted-destination list, and Restricted information must not be accessed from outside the UK unless the CISO has approved it in writing and the customer contract permits it.

- Requests for more than 10 working days are exceptions that require Director of People Operations approval and external tax and immigration advice; no exception may exceed 20 working days in a rolling 12-month period.

- Working while on holiday abroad without approval (for example, checking email for a few minutes is acceptable, but joining customer calls or accessing customer systems is not) is a breach of this policy.

Section 2.3 sets out the probation process. Managers must not wait until the final week to raise concerns: concerns must be documented at the month 1 or month 3 review where they arise. The extension must be confirmed in writing before the original probation end date. If no written outcome is issued by the end of the original 6-month period, the employee should contact People Operations; probation is not automatically passed or failed. During probation, the notice period on either side is **1 week** . Annual leave during probation is covered in section 6.16 and company sick pay during probation in section 7.5. If probation is not passed, the manager must hold a meeting with the employee, explain the reasons, give the employee an opportunity to respond, and confirm the outcome in writing.
