testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-029
testCases.input: What conditions must I meet to get Northstar's enhanced maternity pay, and what does it pay?
testCases.actualOutput:
To qualify, you must be eligible for SMP and have at least 26 weeks’ continuous service by the end of the 15th week before your expected week of childbirth (EWC).

- Weeks 1–16: full basic pay, inclusive of SMP.
- Weeks 17–39: SMP only.
- Weeks 40–52: unpaid.
testCases.expectedOutput: Enhanced maternity pay requires that you qualify for SMP (including average weekly earnings of at least £129) and have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the expected week of childbirth. It pays full basic pay (inclusive of SMP) for weeks 1–16, SMP only for weeks 17–39, and nothing for weeks 40–52. If you do not return for at least 6 months after maternity leave, the enhanced element above SMP is repayable, except for redundancy, ill-health capability or a further immediately following period of statutory family leave. Maternity leave itself (52 weeks) is a day-one right.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.1 Maternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Pregnant employees are entitled to up to 52 weeks of Statutory Maternity Leave (26 weeks of Ordinary Maternity Leave and 26 weeks of Additional Maternity Leave), regardless of length of service, hours or pay. The earliest leave can start is 11 weeks before the EWC. Employees must take at least 2 weeks of compulsory maternity leave after the birth.

**Notice.** By the end of the 15th week before the EWC, the employee must tell People Operations (via PeopleHub) that she is pregnant, her EWC and the date she wants maternity leave to start. Northstar will confirm the expected return date in writing within 28 days. To change the return date, the employee must give at least 8 weeks' notice.

**Statutory Maternity Pay.** SMP requires at least 28 days' notice of the date SMP should start and evidence of pregnancy (a MATB1 certificate or a letter from a doctor or midwife) within 21 days of the SMP start date. A MATB1 cannot be issued more than 20 weeks before the due date. Employees who do not qualify for SMP may be able to claim Maternity Allowance from the government; Northstar will issue form SMP1 explaining why SMP is not payable.

**Northstar enhanced maternity pay.** Employees who qualify for SMP **and** have at least 26 weeks' continuous service at the end of the 15th week before the EWC receive:

**Table 8.1 — Northstar enhanced maternity and adoption pay**

|**Weeks of leave**|**Payment**|
|---|---|
|Weeks 1 to 16|Full basic pay, inclusive of SMP or SAP.|
|Weeks 17 to 39|SMP or SAP only.|
|Weeks 40 to 52|Unpaid.|

If the employee does not return to work for at least **6 months** after the end of maternity leave, she must repay the enhanced element (the amount paid above SMP), unless employment ends because of redundancy, ill-health capability, or a further period of statutory family leave immediately following the first. Statutory pay is never repayable because an employee does not return.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.4 Shared parental leave and pay

Eligible parents can share up to **50 weeks** of leave and up to **37 weeks** of pay by ending maternity or adoption leave early. Eligibility depends on both parents: the employee must meet the continuity of employment test (normally 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or by the week of matching, and still employed in the first week of shared parental leave), and the other parent must meet the employment and earnings test. The employee must give at least **8 weeks' written notice** of leave dates. Requests for discontinuous blocks may be refused; the employee may then take the leave as one continuous block. Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 7

## Family leave: day-one rights, conditional pay

Paternity leave
Day-one right since 6 April 2026: up to 2 weeks. Full pay for 2 weeks only if the employee qualifies for SPP (26 weeks' service by the qualifying week); otherwise unpaid.
Unpaid parental leave
Day-one right since 6 April 2026: 18 weeks per child up to age 18, maximum 4 weeks per child per year, 21 days' notice.
Enhanced maternity and adoption pay
16 weeks' full pay, then statutory pay to week 39, for employees who qualify for statutory pay and have 26 weeks' service. Shared parental pay has no enhancement.
Leave and pay are assessed separately: an employee can be entitled to the leave but not to the pay.

Speaker notes: Leave and pay eligibility are assessed separately. Employees can be entitled to leave without being entitled to statutory or enhanced pay. Carer's leave: one week per 12 months from day one, with the first 3 days paid by Northstar. Time off for dependants: Northstar pays up to 2 days per occurrence and up to 5 paid days per leave year.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.7 Pregnancy and adoption appointments

- Pregnant employees have a statutory right to reasonable **paid** time off for antenatal care, including relaxation and parenting classes recommended by a doctor or midwife. After the first appointment, Northstar may ask to see an appointment card and confirmation of pregnancy.

- Partners of a pregnant woman have a statutory right to unpaid time off to accompany her to up to two antenatal appointments, of up to 6.5 hours each. Northstar pays this time in full as a company enhancement.

- Employees adopting a child can take time off for adoption appointments in line with the statutory scheme; Northstar pays this time in full.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.6 Neonatal care leave and pay

Parents whose baby is admitted to neonatal care within 28 days of birth and stays in care for at least 7 full, consecutive days can take up to **12 weeks** of neonatal care leave (one week for each full week the baby spends in neonatal care). Leave is a day-one right and must be taken within 68 weeks of the birth. Statutory Neonatal Care Pay requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service and minimum earnings. Northstar tops up Statutory Neonatal Care Pay to **full basic pay** for employees with at least 26 weeks' continuous service. Neonatal care leave is taken in addition to other family leave.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-031
testCases.input: I've worked here 4 years. Could I take a 2-month sabbatical starting in 14 months' time?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes—if you’ll have at least 5 years’ continuous service when it starts, a 2-month sabbatical is within the permitted 1-to-3-month length. Apply at least 3 months ahead; approval is discretionary and depends on business needs, and you can take one no more than once in any 5-year period.
testCases.expectedOutput: Sabbaticals are discretionary unpaid leave of 1 to 3 months for employees who will have at least 5 years' continuous service on the proposed start date, no more than once in 5 years. Applications must be made at least 3 months before the start and are approved by a Director depending on business needs. In 14 months you will have roughly 5 years and 2 months' service, so you can apply, but approval is not guaranteed; salary, pension contributions and annual leave accrual are suspended during the unpaid period.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.7 Sabbaticals and career breaks

Employees who will have at least **5 years' continuous service** on the proposed start date may apply for an unpaid sabbatical of **1 to 3 months** , no more than once in any 5-year period. Applications must be made at least **3 months** before the proposed start and approved by a Director. Approval is discretionary and depends on business needs. During a sabbatical, employment continues, but salary, pension contributions and annual leave accrual are suspended for the unpaid period; life assurance and private medical insurance continue.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Other leave procedures

## **Worked example 6.1 — jury service**

An employee is summoned for jury service lasting 13 working days in May 2027 and has had no jury service earlier in 2027. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days; the employee must not claim loss of earnings from the court for those days. For the remaining 3 working days Northstar does not pay, and the employee claims loss of earnings from the court.

## **Worked example 6.2 — sabbatical eligibility**

An employee who started on 1 May 2021 applies on 10 April 2026 for a sabbatical starting 1 August 2026. On the start date they would have 5 years and 3 months of service, but on the date of application they have less than 5 years. Eligibility is assessed at the proposed start date, so they are eligible to apply, and the application is made more than 3 months ahead. Approval remains at the Director's discretion.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year)

- **Request submitted Thursday 1 October 2026** for 3 days starting Monday 12 October 2026. Working days between: 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 October = 6. The current rule (10 working days) applies, so this is **short notice** .

- **Part-time 2026 entitlement (3 days per week, 0.6 FTE, less than 5 years' service):** archived allowance 15 days (112.5 hours) plus bank holidays on working days, plus a transitional uplift of 3.75 x 0.6 = **2.25 hours** , giving 114.75 hours of annual leave.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.6 Unpaid personal leave

Unpaid personal leave of up to **10 working days** per leave year may be approved at the Head of Department's discretion, normally only once the employee's annual leave for the year has been used or booked. It is not an entitlement. Requests of more than 10 working days are considered as sabbaticals (section 9.7).

Entitlement and carryover are determined by the leave year. ### **Worked examples 3.9 — transition** - **Request submitted Monday 28 September 2026** for 3 days starting Tuesday 6 October 2026. testCases.input: Will Northstar pay for a taxi home from the station at 22:30 after a client trip?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes, it may be reimbursed: 22:30 falls within the eligible 22:00–06:00 period, provided the taxi was a reasonable, necessary business expense and you have evidence. Reimbursement is capped at £50 per journey; a fare above £50 needs Head of Department approval.
testCases.expectedOutput: Taxis are reimbursable up to £50 per journey where the journey is between 22:00 and 06:00 (among other qualifying reasons). A 22:30 journey after business travel qualifies; above £50 needs Head of Department approval. An itemised receipt is required.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.1 Principles

Northstar reimburses reasonable, necessary expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for Northstar business, where the claim is supported by evidence, submitted on time and approved by the right person. Employees should spend company money as carefully as their own and choose the most cost-effective option that meets the business need.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.6 Taxis and ride-hailing

Taxis are reimbursable up to **£50 per journey** only where: no reasonable public transport is available; the journey is between 22:00 and 06:00; the employee is carrying heavy or valuable equipment; or for personal safety or accessibility reasons. Journeys above £50 need Head of Department approval. Taxis between home and the normal workplace are not reimbursable except between 22:00 and 06:00 after work required by an incident or approved overtime.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 2 Principles and responsibilities - Expenses must be incurred wholly, exclusively and necessarily for Northstar business. - Choose the most cost-effective option that meets the business need, taking account of time, safety and accessibility. - Limits in this policy are maximums, not allowances. Amounts above a limit are not reimbursed unless an exception is approved under section 16; the claimant bears the difference. - Claims must be honest, accurate and supported by evidence. **Table 2.1 — Responsibilities** |**Role**|**Responsibilities**| |---|---| |Claimant|Obtain pre-approval; book through the Travel desk where required; keep itemised receipts; submit
within 30 calendar days; tag customer-rechargeable costs; repay any amount reimbursed in error
within 10 working days.| |Approver|Review within 5 working days; check business purpose, limits, evidence and pre-approval; reject or
query non-compliant items; never approve own claims or where conflicted.| |Finance (Expenses team)|Validate claims, apply limits and exchange rates, audit a sample of at least 10% of claims monthly,
operate duplicate detection, process reimbursement, and report fraud indicators.| |Travel desk|Book rail, flights and hotels within policy; maintain the travel-risk register; support travellers in an
emergency.|

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.11 Pension

Northstar automatically enrols eligible employees into the Northstar Group Personal Pension, in line with workplace pension auto-enrolment law. The statutory minimum total contribution is 8% of qualifying earnings (at least 3% from the employer), where qualifying earnings for 2026/27 are earnings between £6,240 and £50,270 a year. Northstar contributes **5% of basic salary** when the employee contributes at least **4% of basic salary** ; contributions can be made by salary sacrifice. Employees may opt out, but will then lose the employer contribution, and Northstar will re-enrol eligible employees periodically as the law requires.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.9 Client entertainment

Client entertainment must have a clear business purpose and be pre-approved by the Head of Department. The limit is **£60 per head** , including drinks, for all attendees (Northstar and client). More than £100 per head requires Director pre-approval and an entry in the gifts and hospitality register within 5 working days. The claim must list all attendees, their organisations and the business purpose. Entertainment of public officials requires prior approval from the Head of Risk and Compliance. Entertainment of anyone involved in an active tender with Northstar is prohibited.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-034
testCases.input: Can I carry over more than 5 days of leave this year?
testCases.actualOutput:
Yes. For 2026, the standard carryover limit is 5 days, but exceptions can allow more.
- If sickness prevented you taking leave, up to 20 days (pro-rated for part-time) can carry over in addition to the standard 5; it’s automatic with evidence and must be used within 18 months after the end of 2026.
- If family-related leave prevented you taking leave, all unused annual leave for the year carries over automatically and must be used within 12 months of your return to work.
- For exceptional business reasons, a further 5 days can be carried over, up to 10 days total; request by 30 November and get Director of People Operations approval, then use it by 30 June 2027.
testCases.expectedOutput: The standard limit is 5 days, used by 31 March. More can be carried only if: (a) sickness prevented you taking leave — up to 4 weeks extra, to be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year; (b) family-related leave prevented it — all untaken leave, to be used within 12 months of return; or (c) the company asked you to defer for business reasons — a further 5 days (10 total), requested by 30 November, approved by the Director of People Operations, used by 30 June. Exceptions are not automatic and not precedents.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-038
testCases.input: I support a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data). Can I work from Italy for a week?
testCases.actualOutput: Potentially, if Italy is not on IT Security’s restricted-destination list and you meet the eligibility and approval requirements. You must not access Restricted data unless the CISO approves in writing and the customer contract permits it; otherwise, your Restricted-data tasks need UK-based cover. Submit the request at least 4 weeks ahead and get approval from your line manager, People Operations and IT Security.
testCases.expectedOutput: Work From Abroad is allowed for up to 10 working days in any rolling 12 months for employees past probation and not under notice, with a PeopleHub request at least 4 weeks ahead approved by the line manager, People Operations and IT Security, and not to restricted destinations. Separately, the security policy prohibits accessing Restricted information from outside the UK unless the CISO has approved in writing and the customer contract permits it. So you could work abroad only on non-Restricted tasks, with a UK colleague covering the payroll work, unless that written approval exists.
retrievalContext:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Working from outside the UK > 7.3 Worked examples

## **Work From Abroad examples**

- **Within the limit:** An employee who has not worked abroad in the past 12 months requests to work from Portugal for 5 working days in July 2027, submitting the request 6 weeks ahead. Approvable, subject to all three approvals.

- **Rolling limit exceeded:** An employee worked abroad for 6 days in February 2027 and asks for 5 days in October 2027. Within the rolling 12 months this would total 11 days, so only **4 days** can be approved unless the Director of People Operations approves an exception (maximum 20 days).

- **Restricted customer data:** An employee who supports a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data) asks to work from Italy for a week. They may work abroad only on tasks that do not involve Restricted data, unless the CISO approves in writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK. The manager arranges UK-based cover for Restricted tasks.

- **Short notice:** A request submitted 10 days before travel does not meet the 4-week notice requirement and will normally be declined.

- **Probation:** An employee in month 4 of probation asks to work from Spain for 3 days. Not eligible until probation is completed.

- **Holiday email:** An employee on annual leave in France briefly reads email on their phone. This is not a working day abroad. Joining a customer call or accessing customer systems would be, and requires approval.

10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.8 Working overseas and cross-border working

Working from outside the UK raises tax, social security, immigration, insurance, employment-law and data-protection risks for both the employee and Northstar.

- Employees who have completed probation and are not serving notice may work temporarily from another country for up to **10 working days** in any rolling 12-month period, only with prior approval through the "Work From Abroad" request in PeopleHub, submitted at least **4 weeks** before travel and approved by the line manager, People Operations and IT Security.

- Work from abroad is not permitted from countries on the IT Security restricted-destination list, and Restricted information must not be accessed from outside the UK unless the CISO has approved it in writing and the customer contract permits it.

- Requests for more than 10 working days are exceptions that require Director of People Operations approval and external tax and immigration advice; no exception may exceed 20 working days in a rolling 12-month period.

- Working while on holiday abroad without approval (for example, checking email for a few minutes is acceptable, but joining customer calls or accessing customer systems is not) is a breach of this policy.

Full rules and examples are in NDS-HR-HFW-005 section 7.

7 Working from outside the UK > 7.2 Why the limits exist

Working abroad can create tax and social security liabilities for the employee and Northstar, may require a work permit or visa even for remote work, may give rise to local employment-law obligations, may not be covered by Northstar's insurance, and may breach customer contracts or data-protection requirements on international transfers. Employees are responsible for having the right to enter the country; People Operations' screening does not amount to immigration or tax advice to the individual.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-039
testCases.input: I'm a G2 engineer and I've just resigned. I have 5 days of approved leave booked for after my last day. What happens?
testCases.actualOutput: Your final holiday balance subtracts leave taken or booked up to your leaving date, so these five days booked after that date aren’t included in that calculation. Any positive balance is paid; a negative balance may be deducted where your contract permits. The policy doesn’t say whether the bookings are automatically cancelled, so check with People Operations about that.
testCases.expectedOutput: As a G2 after probation your contractual notice is 1 month. Approved leave that falls after your leaving date is cancelled automatically. Your final holiday balance is the pro-rated entitlement to the leaving date plus valid carryover minus leave taken or booked; positive balances are paid at annual basic salary / 260 per day, and over-taken leave is deducted where the contract permits. You may ask to take leave during your notice period, and Northstar may require you to take accrued leave during notice by giving notice of at least twice the length of that leave. Final adjustments are paid per the final pay timing rule (section 22.11).

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

testCases.input: Can I take 3 days off during a customer go-live that my Head of Department has published as a critical delivery period?
testCases.actualOutput: You can request it, but leave during a published critical delivery period needs both line manager and Head of Department approval and is normally approved only in exceptional circumstances.
testCases.expectedOutput: Critical delivery periods must be published at least 6 weeks ahead, last at most 15 working days and no more than 2 per team per year. Leave within one requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval and is normally approved only in exceptional circumstances (for example, a family wedding booked before publication). The normal 10-working-day notice for 2–5 days still applies. Leave approved before publication remains approved and can only be cancelled by the company in exceptional circumstances with re-credit and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.7 Critical delivery periods and team coverage

A Head of Department may publish a critical delivery period in PeopleHub at least 6 weeks before it starts, lasting no more than 15 working days, with no more than 2 per team per leave year. During that period, annual leave also requires Head of Department approval and is approved only exceptionally (for example, a family wedding booked before the period was published, or compassionate reasons). Leave approved before publication stays approved unless cancelled under handbook section 6.13, with re-credit of the leave and reimbursement of evidenced non-refundable costs.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.7 Manager response, team coverage and critical delivery periods

- Managers must approve or decline a request in PeopleHub within **5 working days** of submission. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub automatically escalates the request to the Head of Department. A request is not approved by default because a manager did not respond.

- Unless the Head of Department approves otherwise, no more than **30% of a team** (rounded down, with a minimum of one person) may be on planned annual leave on the same working day. For a team of 8 this is 2 people; for a team of 3 it is 1 person.

- A Head of Department may designate a **critical delivery period** (for example, a customer go-live, a data-centre migration or the Finance year-end close) by publishing it in PeopleHub at least **6 weeks** before it starts. A critical delivery period may last no more than **15 working days** , and no team may have more than **2** critical delivery periods in a leave year.

- Annual leave requested for dates within a published critical delivery period requires Head of Department approval in addition to line manager approval, and will normally be approved only in exceptional circumstances.

- Leave that was already approved before a critical delivery period was published remains approved. It can only be cancelled by the company under section 6.13.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.10 Company shutdown

Three days are reserved each year for the shutdown between Christmas and New Year: 29 to 31 December 2026 and 29 to 31 December 2027. Part-time employees reserve only the shutdown days that fall on their working days. Employees rostered to work during the shutdown take the equivalent leave at another time agreed with their manager.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.14 Company shutdown Northstar closes its offices for 3 working days between Christmas and New Year. Employees must reserve **3 days** of annual leave for the shutdown (or the shutdown days that fall on their working days, for part-time employees). Shutdown dates are published by **31 January** each year. **Table 6.14 — Company shutdown dates** |**Leave year**|**Shutdown dates**|**Days to reserve (full-time)**| |---|---|---| |2026|Tuesday 29, Wednesday 30 and Thursday 31
December 2026|3 days| |2027|Wednesday 29, Thursday 30 and Friday 31
December 2027|3 days| Employees on the customer support or on-call rota during the shutdown work as rostered and take the equivalent leave at another time. New starters with insufficient leave may take unpaid leave for the shutdown or, with manager agreement, work remotely.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.6 Requesting and approving leave **Table 3.6 — Minimum notice and approvals (requests submitted on or after 1 October 2026)** |**Length of leave**|**Minimum notice (working**
**days)**|**Approval**| |---|---|---| |Up to 1 working day, including hourly and
half-day leave|2|Line manager| |More than 1 and up to 5 working days|10|Line manager| |More than 5 and up to 10 working days|20|Line manager| |More than 10 and up to 15 consecutive working
days|40|Line manager and Head of Department| |More than 15 consecutive working days|40|Line manager, Head of Department and Director| Procedure: 1. The employee submits the request in PeopleHub, adding a note if the dates are linked to religious observance, caring responsibilities or an event that cannot be moved. 2. The line manager checks the balance, team coverage (no more than 30% of the team, rounded down, minimum one person) and any critical delivery period, and decides within **5 working days** . 3. If there is no decision after 5 working days, PeopleHub escalates the request to the Head of Department. Silence is never approval. 4. If declined, the manager records the business reason. The employee may request a Head of Department review within 5 working days; the Head of Department responds within 5 working days. ## **Worked example 3.6 — counting notice** An employee submits a request on Monday 1 February 2027 for 3 days starting Monday 15 February 2027. The working days between the two dates are 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 February = **9 working days** . The minimum is 10, so the request is short notice and may be approved only at the manager's discretion. If the leave started on Tuesday 16 February 2027, there would be 10 working days of notice and the notice requirement would be met.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-041
testCases.input: I'm going from full-time to 22.5 hours (Mon–Wed) on 1 July 2027 and I've already taken 60 hours of leave this year. How is my 2027 leave worked out?
testCases.actualOutput:
The year is split at 1 July: each period’s allowance is prorated by calendar days, then the totals are rounded up to the next 0.25 hour. Bank holidays on your working days are deducted separately: 37.5 hours before July and 22.5 hours after July.

Assuming the 60 hours are annual leave you have already taken, your balance depends on your service band:
- **Under 3 years:** 209.75 hours total allowance; 149.75 hours bookable after bank holidays; **89.75 hours remain** after the 60 hours taken. Reserve 7.5 hours for the 29 December shutdown, leaving 82.25 hours for other leave.
- **3 to under 5 years:** using the 270-hour full-time allowance, **95.75 hours remain** after the bank holiday deductions and 60 hours taken. Reserve 7.5 hours for the shutdown, leaving 88.25 hours for other leave.
- **5 or more years:** using the 277.5-hour full-time allowance, **101.75 hours remain** after the bank holiday deductions and 60 hours taken. Reserve 7.5 hours for the shutdown, leaving 94.25 hours for other leave.
testCases.expectedOutput: Under the changed-hours method you split the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded, add them, round up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays falling on working days. Period 1 (1 Jan–30 Jun, 181 days, full-time): 262.5 x 181/365 = 130.171 h. Period 2 (1 Jul–31 Dec, 184 days, 0.6 FTE): 157.5 x 184/365 = 79.397 h. Total 209.568 → 209.75 h. Bank holidays: period 1 has 5 on working days (37.5 h), period 2 has 3 on Mon–Wed (22.5 h). Bookable = 149.75 h; after 60 h taken, 89.75 h remain, of which 7.5 h is reserved for the shutdown day on Wednesday 29 December 2027.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

## **Worked example 3.4B — part-time to full-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday) from 1 January to 31 March 2027 (90 days), then full-time from 1 April to 31 December 2027 (275 days).

- Period 1: 157.5 x 90 / 365 = 38.836 hours

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

Pro-rated entitlement = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / days in the leave year), rounded up (0.5 day for day-based, 0.25 hour for hours-based).

## **Worked examples 3.5 — joiners**

- **Full-time joiner, 1 March 2027:** 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.636, rounded up to **23.0 days** , plus 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027.

- **Full-time joiner, 16 September 2027:** calendar days 16 September to 31 December = 107. 27 x 107 / 365 = 7.915, rounded up to **8.0 days** , plus the 27 and 28 December bank holidays. Three of these days must be reserved for the 2027 shutdown (29 to 31 December).

- **Part-time joiner, 1 July 2027, 22.5 hours Monday to Wednesday:** 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397, rounded up to **79.5 hours** . Bank holidays on working days (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 22.5 hours. Bookable annual leave = **57.0 hours** .

## **Worked examples 3.5 — leavers**

- **Full-time leaver, 30 June 2027, salary £45,500:** 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Taken 10 days: balance 3.5 days x £175.00 = **£612.50** paid. Taken 15 days: balance −1.5 days x £175.00 = **£262.50** deducted where the contract permits.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

- Period 1: 157.5 x 90 / 365 = 38.836 hours

- Period 2: 262.5 x 275 / 365 = 197.774 hours

- Total: 236.610 hours, rounded up to **236.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days: period 1 (29 Mar) 7.5 hours; period 2 (3 May, 31 May, 30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) 37.5 hours; total 45 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 236.75 − 45 = **191.75 hours**

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours Part-time employees' entitlement is calculated in hours and includes the bank holiday element, so that part-time employees are treated no less favourably than full-time employees, whichever days they work. ## **Part-time entitlement formula** Total annual allowance (hours) = 262.5 hours x (contracted weekly hours / 37.5) 262.5 hours is the full-time total of 35 days (27 annual leave days + 8 bank holidays) x 7.5 hours. For employees with 3 or more years' service the full-time total is 270 hours (36 days); with 5 or more years it is 277.5 hours (37 days). Bank holidays that fall on the employee's normal working days are deducted from the allowance, at the hours the employee would normally have worked that day. The remainder is available to book as annual leave. Rounding: round the total annual allowance up to the nearest 0.25 hour. **Table 6.3 — Part-time allowance examples, 2027 leave year, less than 3 years' service** |**Working pattern**|**FTE**|**Total allowance**
**(hours)**|**Bank holidays on working**
**days in 2027 (hours deducted)**|**Bookable annual leave**
**(hours)**| |---|---|---|---|---| |3 days, Mon–Wed, 7.5 hours per
day (22.5 hours per week)|0.6|157.5|6 days x 7.5 = 45.0|112.5| |4 days, Mon–Thu, 7.5 hours per
day (30 hours per week)|0.8|210.0|6 days x 7.5 = 45.0|165.0| |5 days, Mon–Fri, 6 hours per
day (30 hours per week)|0.8|210.0|8 days x 6 = 48.0|162.0|

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

- **Part-time leaver, 31 March 2027, 30 hours Monday to Thursday, salary £32,000:** 210 x 90 / 365 = 51.781, rounded up to 52.0 hours. Bank holiday on a working day (29 March) = 7.5 hours, leaving 44.5 bookable hours. Taken 30 hours: balance 14.5 hours. Hourly rate = £32,000 / (52 x 30) = £20.5128. Payment = 14.5 x £20.5128 = **£297.44** .

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-042
testCases.input: I'm going to Berlin for 3 nights for a customer workshop. What approvals do I need and how do I claim a taxi I paid for in cash euros?
testCases.actualOutput:
Before travelling internationally, get Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check. Record the approval in ExpenseFlow as a “Travel and spend request” and quote its reference on your claim.

A cash taxi fare in euros is converted using Finance’s published rate for the month of travel; for example, the policy’s Berlin example converts euros to pounds by dividing by the published euros-per-£1 rate. The taxi is reimbursable up to £50 per journey only if a qualifying condition applies, such as no reasonable public transport, travel between 22:00 and 06:00, carrying heavy or valuable equipment, or personal safety or accessibility reasons. Journeys above £50 need Head of Department approval.
testCases.expectedOutput: International travel requires Director pre-approval and a Travel desk travel-risk check before booking, and an overnight stay is involved. Berlin is Band B: hotel up to £200 per night, breakfast £15, lunch £20, dinner £45, daily meal cap £70, incidental £10 per night. Claims are in sterling: card payments use the statement amount including fees; cash uses Finance's published monthly rate for the month of the expense, sterling = foreign amount / rate rounded to the nearest penny (e.g. €30 / 1.16 = £25.86). Itemised receipts are needed and the claim must be submitted within 30 days; a total over £250 requires line manager and Head of Department approval.
retrievalContext:
Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.6 Taxis and ride-hailing

Taxis are reimbursable up to **£50 per journey** only where: no reasonable public transport is available; the journey is between 22:00 and 06:00; the employee is carrying heavy or valuable equipment; or for personal safety or accessibility reasons. Journeys above £50 need Head of Department approval. Taxis between home and the normal workplace are not reimbursable except between 22:00 and 06:00 after work required by an incident or approved overtime.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.7 Parking, tolls and charges

Parking at customer sites, stations and airports (for trips of up to 3 nights) is reimbursable at actual cost with a receipt or app record. Tolls, the London Congestion Charge and Clean Air Zone or ULEZ charges for business journeys are reimbursable where use of a car was justified. Penalty charge notices, parking fines and speeding fines are never reimbursable.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.4 — crossing the 10,000-mile threshold**

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

# **Example 14.7 — late claims and reimbursement dates**

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.1 — two-day London trip**

A Manchester-based consultant travels to London on Tuesday and returns Wednesday, with an approved overnight stay.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-043
testCases.input: I got ill on the second day of my holiday in New York. What should I do to get my leave back?
testCases.actualOutput:
Contact your line manager about the sickness on its first day; because you’re in a different time zone, report it as soon as reasonably practicable. Call your manager as set out in the reporting rules.
Provide self-certification for an absence of up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note if it lasts more than 7 calendar days.
Your manager can reclassify the affected days in PeopleHub so they’re re-credited to your leave balance. Days reported only after you return from holiday are not normally reclassified.
testCases.expectedOutput: Sickness during annual leave can be reclassified and re-credited if you report it on the first day of sickness by calling your line manager by 09:30, or as soon as reasonably practicable if you are in a different time zone, and provide evidence: self-certification for up to 7 calendar days or a fit note for more than 7. Sickness reported only after you return is not normally reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.12 Sickness during annual leave

An employee who falls ill during annual leave may have the affected days reclassified as sickness absence and re-credited to their annual leave balance, provided that they:

1. report the sickness to their line manager by **09:30** on the first day of sickness (or as soon as reasonably practicable if they are in a different time zone), following section 7.1; and

2. provide self-certification for absences of up to 7 calendar days, or a fit note for absences of more than 7 calendar days, as set out in section 7.3.

Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence under section 7.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.11 Sickness during annual leave

Report sickness by 09:30 on the first day of sickness under section 4.1, even while on leave. Provide self-certification (1 to 7 calendar days) or a fit note (more than 7 calendar days). The manager reclassifies the days in PeopleHub and the leave is re-credited. Sickness reported only after returning from leave is not normally reclassified.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.7 Return to work and phased return

Return-to-work conversations take place within 2 working days of return. Phased returns of up to 4 weeks are on full pay; longer phased returns need Head of Department approval, with the balance of hours covered by annual leave or remaining company sick pay.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.2 Evidence

Self-certification covers up to 7 calendar days (including non-working days). A fit note is required for absences of more than 7 calendar days, submitted within 3 working days of issue. Northstar may require fit notes for all absences once an employee reaches Stage 1 of the attendance process and will reimburse any charge.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.1 Reporting an absence

### **How to report sickness**

1. **Call** your line manager (telephone or Teams voice/video call) no later than **09:30** on the first day of absence. Shift workers and employees on an on-call rota must call at least **1 hour before** their shift or rota period starts. 2. If your line manager is unavailable, call your Head of Department or team lead. Leaving a voicemail is acceptable only if you also send a message and follow up with a call before 12:00. 3. Text messages, emails or chat messages alone are not sufficient, except where you are physically unable to speak; in that case, send a message and call as soon as you are able. 4. Record the absence in PeopleHub on the same day, or ask your manager to do so on your behalf. 5. Tell your manager the reason for absence in general terms, your expected return date, and any work that needs urgent cover. You do not have to disclose a diagnosis.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-044
testCases.input: I'm a remote employee and my last day is Friday 20 November 2026. What are my deadlines for returning equipment and submitting expenses, when is my access cut off, and when will my final holiday pay arrive?
testCases.actualOutput: Return your equipment by Friday 27 November 2026, within 5 working days after your leaving date. Submit outstanding expenses by Friday 4 December 2026, within 10 working days after leaving. Your system and building access will be revoked at 17:30 on Friday 20 November. Because your leaving date is after the 10th, your final holiday pay is due on 25 December 2026.
testCases.expectedOutput: Remote or hybrid leavers return equipment within 5 working days after the leaving date: 23–27 November, so by Friday 27 November 2026. Expense claims must be submitted within 10 working days after the leaving date: by Friday 4 December 2026. System and building access is revoked at 17:30 on the last working day. Because the leaving date is after the 10th, November salary is paid as normal on 25 November and final adjustments are paid on the 25th of the following month; 25 December 2026 is Christmas Day (a bank holiday), so payment is on the previous working day, Thursday 24 December 2026.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.6 Returning equipment

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

- **Remote or hybrid leavers** return all equipment within **5 working days** after their leaving date, using the prepaid courier arranged by IT. Access cards may be posted with the equipment.

- If equipment has not been returned within **10 working days** after the leaving date, IT escalates to People Operations, who send a written reminder and may take recovery action. Any deduction from final pay is made only where the contract permits or the employee has agreed in writing.

- Employees returning from long-term absence or moving role return any equipment no longer needed within 10 working days of IT's request.

6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

testCases.input: A customer made sexual comments to me during a meeting at their site. What can I do and how fast must I report it?
testCases.actualOutput: You may end the meeting or leave the site if you feel unsafe, and you won’t be penalized for ending the interaction in good faith. Treat this as a Severity 2 incident: report it to your line manager and People Operations within 1 hour, and follow the customer’s site incident procedure as well as Northstar’s reporting process.
testCases.expectedOutput: Northstar protects employees from harassment by customers and third parties. You may end the call or meeting, or leave the location if you feel unsafe, and you will not be penalised for doing so in good faith. Harassment from a customer is Severity 2: report to your line manager and the relevant team within 1 hour. Record what happened and keep evidence. Your manager will ensure you are safe, offer support and escalate to the Account Director and People Operations; Northstar will raise it with the customer and may change staffing or suspend services.

Employees can raise concerns informally or formally:

- **Informal:** speak to the person directly if you feel able, or ask your line manager, a People Operations partner or a Respect at Work Contact to help resolve the matter informally.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-047
testCases.input: I've been summoned for jury service during my team's critical delivery period. Do I have to go, and will I be paid?
testCases.actualOutput:
Northstar must allow you time off for jury service. If your absence would seriously harm the business, it may ask you to apply to defer; it must give you a letter explaining why, and jury service can be deferred only once in a 12-month period.

Northstar pays your full basic pay for the first 10 working days in a leave year; after that, the time is unpaid by Northstar, and you may claim loss of earnings from the court. Tell your line manager and upload a copy of your summons to PeopleHub within 2 working days of receiving it.
testCases.expectedOutput: Jury service is a statutory right to time off, not annual leave, so critical-delivery-period rules on annual leave do not apply. Tell your manager and upload the summons within 2 working days. If the absence would seriously harm the business Northstar may ask you to apply to defer, giving you a letter; deferral is possible only once in 12 months. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days in a leave year (do not claim loss of earnings for those days); after that it is unpaid and you claim loss of earnings from the court.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.3 Jury service

Northstar must allow employees time off for jury service. Employees must tell their line manager and upload a copy of the summons to PeopleHub within **2 working days** of receiving it. If the absence would seriously harm the business, Northstar may ask the employee to apply to defer jury service, giving the employee a letter explaining why; jury service can be deferred only once in a 12-month period. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first **10 working days** of jury service in any leave year; the employee must not claim loss of earnings from the court for those days. After 10 working days, jury service is unpaid by Northstar and the employee may claim loss of earnings from the court using the court's employer form, which People Operations will complete.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Other leave procedures

## **Worked example 6.1 — jury service**

An employee is summoned for jury service lasting 13 working days in May 2027 and has had no jury service earlier in 2027. Northstar pays full basic pay for the first 10 working days; the employee must not claim loss of earnings from the court for those days. For the remaining 3 working days Northstar does not pay, and the employee claims loss of earnings from the court.

## **Worked example 6.2 — sabbatical eligibility**

An employee who started on 1 May 2021 applies on 10 April 2026 for a sabbatical starting 1 August 2026. On the start date they would have 5 years and 3 months of service, but on the date of application they have less than 5 years. Eligibility is assessed at the proposed start date, so they are eligible to apply, and the application is made more than 3 months ahead. Approval remains at the Director's discretion.

**Table 4.4 — Company sick pay (inclusive of SSP) in any rolling 12 months**

|**Continuous service on first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed, less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more, less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-048
testCases.input: I'm starting a hybrid role on 1 March 2027. How often must I be in the office at first, how much leave can I book by June, and when can I claim the home office allowance?
testCases.actualOutput: For your first 4 weeks, you must attend at least 3 days per week. The available policy sources don’t specify how much leave you can book by June or when you can claim a home office allowance; contact People Operations for those details.
testCases.expectedOutput: New starters in hybrid roles attend at least 3 days a week for their first 4 weeks, then follow the standard of 8 days per rolling 4-week period. During probation you may book accrued leave (27 x 3/12 = 6.75, rounded up to 7.0 days on 1 June) plus up to 2 days with manager approval: 9.0 days; more than 5 consecutive days also needs Head of Department approval. The £300 home office allowance is available only after completing the 6-month probation, i.e. from 1 September 2027 if probation is passed on time.

testCases.input: I'm pregnant and have had several pregnancy-related sick days. Will they count towards attendance triggers?
testCases.actualOutput: No. Pregnancy-related sickness absence is excluded from attendance triggers.
testCases.expectedOutput: Pregnancy-related sickness is recorded separately and never counted towards attendance triggers or used in performance, promotion or redundancy decisions. You have a statutory right to reasonable paid time off for antenatal care, and your manager should carry out a pregnancy risk assessment. If you are off with a pregnancy-related illness in the 4 weeks before the expected week of childbirth, maternity leave and pay may start automatically.

4 Sickness absence > 4.5 Attendance review triggers

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.9 Disability, pregnancy and mental health

- **Disability-related absence:** handled with reasonable adjustments (section 4.3). Absence connected with an agreed adjustment (for example, scheduled treatment) may be recorded as disability leave rather than sickness absence.

- **Pregnancy-related sickness:** recorded separately and never counted towards attendance triggers or used in decisions about performance, promotion or redundancy. If a pregnant employee is absent with a pregnancy-related illness in the 4 weeks before the expected week of childbirth, maternity leave and pay may start automatically (see section 8.1).

- **Mental health:** treated in the same way as physical illness. Employees can access the Employee Assistance Programme (Appendix B) and agree a Wellness Action Plan with their manager.

6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.12 Sickness during annual leave

An employee who falls ill during annual leave may have the affected days reclassified as sickness absence and re-credited to their annual leave balance, provided that they:

Days of sickness reported only after the employee returns from leave will not normally be reclassified. Reclassified days are paid as sickness absence under section 7.

testCases.input: I work 3 days a week (Mon–Wed, 7.5 hours a day) and have less than 3 years' service. How many hours of annual leave can I book in 2027?
testCases.actualOutput: You can book **112.5 hours** of annual leave in 2027, after deducting bank holidays that fall on your working days.
testCases.expectedOutput: Part-time allowance = 262.5 x (22.5 / 37.5) = 157.5 hours including bank holidays. In 2027 six bank holidays fall on Monday–Wednesday (29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May, 30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 6 x 7.5 = 45 hours. Bookable annual leave = 157.5 − 45 = 112.5 hours (15 days of 7.5 hours).
retrievalContext:

3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

## **Worked example 3.4B — part-time to full-time**

Pro-rated annual leave = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / total days in the leave year) Count calendar days inclusive of the start date and the leaving date. The leave year has 365 days (366 in a leap year; 2028 is the next leap year).

Rounding for full-time employees: round up to the nearest 0.5 day. Rounding for part-time employees (hours-based): round up to the nearest 0.25 hour.

Full-time joiners and leavers also receive, as paid days off, the bank holidays that fall during their employment. Part-time joiners and leavers use the hours-based allowance in section 6.3, pro-rated in the same way.

- **Joiner example:** a full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 306 (1 March to 31 December inclusive). 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.64 days, rounded up to **23.0 days** of annual leave, plus the 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027 onwards.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-052
testCases.input: A full-time employee earning £45,500 leaves on 30 June 2027 having taken 10 days of leave and with no carryover. What holiday pay is due?
testCases.actualOutput: Holiday pay due is **£612.50 gross**: 13.5 days’ pro-rated entitlement minus 10 days taken leaves 3.5 days, paid at £175 per day.
testCases.expectedOutput: Pro-rated entitlement = 27 x 181/365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Daily rate = £45,500 / 260 = £175.00. Payment = 3.5 x £175.00 = £612.50 gross. Because 30 June is after the 10th, it is paid with final adjustments on 25 July 2027.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.17 Termination and final holiday balance

### **Final holiday balance formula**

Final balance (days) = pro-rated entitlement for the leave year up to the leaving date (section 6.4) + valid carried-over leave − leave taken or booked up to the leaving date

Daily rate for payment or deduction (full-time) = annual basic salary / 260

Hourly rate for payment or deduction (part-time and hours-based calculations) = annual basic salary / (52 x contracted weekly hours)

**Example — positive balance.** A full-time employee earning £45,500 per year leaves on 30 June 2027 with no carried-over leave and has taken 10 days. Pro-rated entitlement = 13.5 days (section 6.4). Balance = 13.5 − 10 = 3.5 days. Payment = 3.5 x (£45,500 / 260) = 3.5 x £175.00 = **£612.50** gross, paid in the final salary payment.

**Example — negative balance.** If the same employee had taken 15 days, the balance would be 13.5 − 15 = −1.5 days. Deduction = 1.5 x £175.00 = **£262.50** gross, deducted from final pay where the contract permits (section 6.16).

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

- **Part-time leaver, 31 March 2027, 30 hours Monday to Thursday, salary £32,000:** 210 x 90 / 365 = 51.781, rounded up to 52.0 hours. Bank holiday on a working day (29 March) = 7.5 hours, leaving 44.5 bookable hours. Taken 30 hours: balance 14.5 hours. Hourly rate = £32,000 / (52 x 30) = £20.5128. Payment = 14.5 x £20.5128 = **£297.44** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

Pro-rated entitlement = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / days in the leave year), rounded up (0.5 day for day-based, 0.25 hour for hours-based).

## **Worked examples 3.5 — joiners**

- **Full-time joiner, 1 March 2027:** 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.636, rounded up to **23.0 days** , plus 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027.

- **Full-time joiner, 16 September 2027:** calendar days 16 September to 31 December = 107. 27 x 107 / 365 = 7.915, rounded up to **8.0 days** , plus the 27 and 28 December bank holidays. Three of these days must be reserved for the 2027 shutdown (29 to 31 December).

- **Part-time joiner, 1 July 2027, 22.5 hours Monday to Wednesday:** 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397, rounded up to **79.5 hours** . Bank holidays on working days (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 22.5 hours. Bookable annual leave = **57.0 hours** .

## **Worked examples 3.5 — leavers**

- **Full-time leaver, 30 June 2027, salary £45,500:** 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Taken 10 days: balance 3.5 days x £175.00 = **£612.50** paid. Taken 15 days: balance −1.5 days x £175.00 = **£262.50** deducted where the contract permits.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.3 Part-time employees and changes to working hours

In 2027 the bank holidays in England and Wales fall on Friday 1 January, Friday 26 March, Monday 29 March, Monday 3 May, Monday 31 May, Monday 30 August, Monday 27 December and Tuesday 28 December. An employee working Monday to Wednesday therefore has 6 bank holidays on working days (29 March, 3 May, 31 May, 30 August, 27 December and 28 December).

**Changes to working hours part-way through the leave year.** Where contracted hours change during the leave year, divide the leave year into periods at the date of change. Calculate the allowance for each period as: (annual allowance in hours for that working pattern) x (calendar days in the period / days in the leave year). Add the unrounded results together and then round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour. Deduct bank holidays that fell on working days in each period at the hours worked on that day in that period. Leave already taken in the first period is deducted from the new total. Worked examples are in NDS-HR-LAS-002 section 3.4.

Compressed hours employees (for example, 37.5 hours worked over 4 days) are 1.0 FTE and receive 262.5 hours, with each bank holiday on a working day deducted at the length of that working day (9.375 hours on a 4-day compressed week).

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.11 Final pay and outstanding annual leave

Salary is paid for the calendar month on the 25th (section 11.1). If the leaving date is **on or before** the 10th of a month, all final pay, including payment for untaken annual leave, approved expenses and any deductions, is paid on the 25th of that month. If the leaving date is **after** the 10th, normal salary for that month is paid on the 25th and the final adjustments (holiday pay, expenses and deductions) are paid on the 25th of the following month. The final holiday balance is calculated as set out in section 6.17.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-054
testCases.input: An employee in probation, whose normal weekly earnings are above £154.07, is off sick for 4 working days (5-day week). How much sick pay do they receive?
testCases.actualOutput: They receive **£98.60 in SSP** for the 4 working days; employees in probation receive SSP only, with no company sick pay.
testCases.expectedOutput: During probation only SSP is paid. SSP is payable from the first day since 6 April 2026 at £123.25 a week (lower than 80% of earnings above £154.07). Daily rate = £123.25 / 5 qualifying days = £24.65. 4 days x £24.65 = £98.60.
retrievalContext:

4 Sickness absence > 4.4 Company sick pay

**Table 4.4 — Company sick pay (inclusive of SSP) in any rolling 12 months**

|**Continuous service on first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed, less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more, less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.3 Statutory Sick Pay

From 6 April 2026, SSP is payable from the first qualifying day of sickness at the lower of £123.25 per week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days are contracted working days. The daily SSP rate is the weekly rate divided by the number of qualifying days in the week.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.4 Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)

## **Statutory Sick Pay from 6 April 2026**

Following the Employment Rights Act 2025, from 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness absence (the former 3 unpaid "waiting days" were removed) and the lower earnings limit no longer applies to eligibility. The weekly rate is £123.25 or 80% of the employee's normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days for SSP are the employee's contracted working days. SSP rates are set by government and usually change each April.

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)

Pregnancy-related absence never counts towards triggers

testCases.actualOutput: You can claim **£45.00**: the first 50 miles at 55p per mile, then the remaining 70 miles at 25p per mile.
testCases.expectedOutput: Only 50 miles remain at the 55p rate before the 10,000-mile threshold; the other 70 are at 25p: 50 x £0.55 = £27.50; 70 x £0.25 = £17.50; total £45.00.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-058
testCases.input: On Monday 1 February 2027 I asked for 3 days off starting Monday 15 February 2027. Did I give enough notice?
testCases.actualOutput: No. You gave 9 working days’ notice, short of the 10 required for 3 days of leave; it may still be approved at your manager’s discretion.
testCases.expectedOutput: Notice counts working days between submission and the first day of leave, excluding both: 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 February = 9 working days. Leave of more than 1 and up to 5 days needs 10 working days, so this is short notice; the manager may still approve at their discretion. Starting on Tuesday 16 February would have given 10.

testCases.input: I'm full-time and took 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period. How many office days do I need in that period? And what if I worked 3 days a week?
testCases.actualOutput: With a full-time schedule, you need **6 office days** in the 4-week period. If you work 3 days a week and also took 5 days of annual leave, you need **3 office days**.
testCases.expectedOutput: Absence reduces the requirement proportionally, rounded up to a whole day: 8 x (15 available / 20 normal working days) = 6 days. For a part-time 3-day week the normal requirement is 8 x 3/5 = 4.8, rounded up to 5 days per rolling 4-week period.
retrievalContext:
Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Office attendance standard > 4.3 Part-time employees and absence

The requirement is pro-rated and rounded **up** to the nearest whole day:

- **Part-time:** required days = 8 x (contracted working days per week / 5). For a 3-day week: 8 x 3 / 5 = 4.8, rounded up to **5 days** per rolling 4-week period.

- **Annual leave, sickness, bank holidays and other approved absence:** required days = (normal requirement) x (available working days in the period / normal working days in the period). For a full-time employee with 5 days of annual leave in a 4-week period of 20 working days: 8 x 15 / 20 = **6 days** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

- Bookable annual leave for 2027: 209.75 − 37.5 − 22.5 = **149.75 hours**

- If the employee took 60 hours of annual leave in period 1, the remaining balance from 1 July is 149.75 − 60 = **89.75 hours** , of which 7.5 hours must be reserved for the shutdown day that falls on a working day (Wednesday 29 December 2027).

## **Worked example 3.4B — part-time to full-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday) from 1 January to 31 March 2027 (90 days), then full-time from 1 April to 31 December 2027 (275 days).

- Period 1: 157.5 x 90 / 365 = 38.836 hours

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-060
testCases.input: Northstar is dismissing a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. How much notice must they give?
testCases.actualOutput: Northstar must give 9 weeks’ notice, because the statutory minimum for 9 complete years of service is longer than the G2 contractual notice of 1 month. The individual employment contract prevails if it provides a longer notice period.
testCases.expectedOutput: Northstar must give the greater of contractual notice (1 month for G1–G3 after probation) and statutory notice (1 week per complete year of service from 2 years, up to 12 weeks). 9 years = 9 weeks, which is longer than 1 month, so 9 weeks' notice is required. testCases.input: A full-time employee joins on 16 September 2027. How much annual leave do they get for 2027?
testCases.actualOutput: They get 8.0 days of pro-rated annual leave, plus the 27 and 28 December bank holidays. Three days of the annual leave must be reserved for the 29–31 December shutdown.
