retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
6 Annual leave and public holidays > 6.4 Joining or leaving during the leave year

## **Joiner and leaver formula**

Pro-rated annual leave = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / total days in the leave year) Count calendar days inclusive of the start date and the leaving date. The leave year has 365 days (366 in a leap year; 2028 is the next leap year).

Rounding for full-time employees: round up to the nearest 0.5 day. Rounding for part-time employees (hours-based): round up to the nearest 0.25 hour.

Full-time joiners and leavers also receive, as paid days off, the bank holidays that fall during their employment. Part-time joiners and leavers use the hours-based allowance in section 6.3, pro-rated in the same way.

- **Joiner example:** a full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 306 (1 March to 31 December inclusive). 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.64 days, rounded up to **23.0 days** of annual leave, plus the 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027 onwards.

- **Leaver example:** a full-time employee with less than 3 years' service leaves on 30 June 2027. Calendar days employed in 2027 = 181. 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.39 days, rounded up to **13.5 days** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

Pro-rated entitlement = annual entitlement x (calendar days employed in the leave year / days in the leave year), rounded up (0.5 day for day-based, 0.25 hour for hours-based).

## **Worked examples 3.5 — joiners**

- **Full-time joiner, 1 March 2027:** 27 x 306 / 365 = 22.636, rounded up to **23.0 days** , plus 7 bank holidays from 26 March 2027.

- **Full-time joiner, 16 September 2027:** calendar days 16 September to 31 December = 107. 27 x 107 / 365 = 7.915, rounded up to **8.0 days** , plus the 27 and 28 December bank holidays. Three of these days must be reserved for the 2027 shutdown (29 to 31 December).

- **Part-time joiner, 1 July 2027, 22.5 hours Monday to Wednesday:** 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397, rounded up to **79.5 hours** . Bank holidays on working days (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec) = 22.5 hours. Bookable annual leave = **57.0 hours** .

## **Worked examples 3.5 — leavers**

- **Full-time leaver, 30 June 2027, salary £45,500:** 27 x 181 / 365 = 13.389, rounded up to 13.5 days. Taken 10 days: balance 3.5 days x £175.00 = **£612.50** paid. Taken 15 days: balance −1.5 days x £175.00 = **£262.50** deducted where the contract permits.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.5 Joiners and leavers

- **Part-time leaver, 31 March 2027, 30 hours Monday to Thursday, salary £32,000:** 210 x 90 / 365 = 51.781, rounded up to 52.0 hours. Bank holiday on a working day (29 March) = 7.5 hours, leaving 44.5 bookable hours. Taken 30 hours: balance 14.5 hours. Hourly rate = £32,000 / (52 x 30) = £20.5128. Payment = 14.5 x £20.5128 = **£297.44** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year)

- **Request submitted Thursday 1 October 2026** for 3 days starting Monday 12 October 2026. Working days between: 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 October = 6. The current rule (10 working days) applies, so this is **short notice** .

- **Part-time 2026 entitlement (3 days per week, 0.6 FTE, less than 5 years' service):** archived allowance 15 days (112.5 hours) plus bank holidays on working days, plus a transitional uplift of 3.75 x 0.6 = **2.25 hours** , giving 114.75 hours of annual leave.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.4 Changes to working hours during the leave year

Divide the leave year at the date of change, calculate each period unrounded as (annual allowance for that pattern) x (calendar days in period / days in year), add the periods, round the total up to the nearest 0.25 hour, then deduct bank holidays on working days for each period.

## **Worked example 3.4A — full-time to part-time**

An employee with less than 3 years' service works full-time (37.5 hours, Monday to Friday) from 1 January to 30 June 2027 (181 days) and 22.5 hours (Monday to Wednesday, 7.5 hours per day) from 1 July to 31 December 2027 (184 days).

- Period 1: 262.5 x 181 / 365 = 130.171 hours

- Period 2: 157.5 x 184 / 365 = 79.397 hours

- Total: 209.568 hours, rounded up to **209.75 hours**

- Bank holidays on working days, period 1 (1 Jan, 26 Mar, 29 Mar, 3 May, 31 May): 5 x 7.5 = 37.5 hours

- Bank holidays on working days, period 2 (30 Aug, 27 Dec, 28 Dec): 3 x 7.5 = 22.5 hours

A claim for one trip must be submitted as a single claim. Splitting one trip or one expense across several claims to avoid a threshold is prohibited and is a fraud indicator (section 12). testCases.input: How much notice must a G5 Engineering Manager give when resigning after probation?

testCases.expectedOutput: Grades G4 and G5 give 2 months' contractual notice after probation.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01) 22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.4 Notice periods **Table 22.4 — Notice periods** |**Situation**|**Notice the employee must give (contractual)**|**Notice Northstar must give**| |---|---|---| |During probation|1 week|1 week| |After probation, grades G1 to G3|1 month|The greater of 1 month and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G4 and G5|2 months|The greater of 2 months and the statutory
minimum| |After probation, grades G6 and G7|3 months|The greater of 3 months and the statutory
minimum| ## **Statutory minimum notice** An employee with more than 1 month's service must give at least 1 week's notice. An employer must give at least 1 week's notice to an employee with between 1 month and 2 years' service, then 1 week for each complete year of service from 2 years, up to a maximum of 12 weeks after 12 years. A contract can give more than these minimums but never less. Notice periods in Table 22.4 are illustrative Northstar contractual terms; the individual employment contract prevails. **Example.** Northstar gives notice to a G2 engineer with 9 complete years of service. Contractual notice is 1 month; statutory notice is 9 weeks. Northstar must give **9 weeks** ' notice because it is longer. testCases.actualOutput: Submit all outstanding expense claims within 10 working days after your leaving date.

22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.8 Outstanding expenses and corporate cards

All outstanding expense claims must be submitted within 10 working days after the leaving date (section 12.3). Corporate cards are cancelled on the last working day; any personal spend or unreconciled amount is recovered as described in section 11.10.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
12 Expenses and business travel > 12.3 Claim deadline and late claims

## **Expense claim deadline**

Submit claims in ExpenseFlow within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted 31 to 90 calendar days after the expense require a written explanation and Head of Department approval. Claims submitted more than 90 calendar days after the expense are not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the employee was on long-term sickness absence). Leavers must submit all claims within **10 working days** after their leaving date.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)

### **Deadlines**

- Submit within **30 calendar days** of the date the expense was incurred. For multi-day trips, each expense's own date applies, but all expenses for one trip should be submitted together within 30 calendar days of the first expense of the trip.

- **31 to 90 calendar days:** a late claim requires a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- **More than 90 calendar days:** not reimbursed, unless the Finance Director approves an exception (for example, where the claimant was on long-term sickness or family leave).

- **Leavers:** all claims must be submitted within **10 working days** after the leaving date. Claims received after that are not paid.

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Working from outside the UK > 7.3 Worked examples

## **Work From Abroad examples**

- **Within the limit:** An employee who has not worked abroad in the past 12 months requests to work from Portugal for 5 working days in July 2027, submitting the request 6 weeks ahead. Approvable, subject to all three approvals.

- **Rolling limit exceeded:** An employee worked abroad for 6 days in February 2027 and asks for 5 days in October 2027. Within the rolling 12 months this would total 11 days, so only **4 days** can be approved unless the Director of People Operations approves an exception (maximum 20 days).

- **Restricted customer data:** An employee who supports a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data) asks to work from Italy for a week. They may work abroad only on tasks that do not involve Restricted data, unless the CISO approves in writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK. The manager arranges UK-based cover for Restricted tasks.

- **Short notice:** A request submitted 10 days before travel does not meet the 4-week notice requirement and will normally be declined.

- **Probation:** An employee in month 4 of probation asks to work from Spain for 3 days. Not eligible until probation is completed.

- **Holiday email:** An employee on annual leave in France briefly reads email on their phone. This is not a working day abroad. Joining a customer call or accessing customer systems would be, and requires approval.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.8 Working overseas and cross-border working

Working from outside the UK raises tax, social security, immigration, insurance, employment-law and data-protection risks for both the employee and Northstar.

- Employees who have completed probation and are not serving notice may work temporarily from another country for up to **10 working days** in any rolling 12-month period, only with prior approval through the "Work From Abroad" request in PeopleHub, submitted at least **4 weeks** before travel and approved by the line manager, People Operations and IT Security.

- Work from abroad is not permitted from countries on the IT Security restricted-destination list, and Restricted information must not be accessed from outside the UK unless the CISO has approved it in writing and the customer contract permits it.

- Requests for more than 10 working days are exceptions that require Director of People Operations approval and external tax and immigration advice; no exception may exceed 20 working days in a rolling 12-month period.

- Working while on holiday abroad without approval (for example, checking email for a few minutes is acceptable, but joining customer calls or accessing customer systems is not) is a breach of this policy.

Full rules and examples are in NDS-HR-HFW-005 section 7.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-077
testCases.input: If I give a colleague a lift to a customer site, can I claim anything extra?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes. You can claim an extra 5p per passenger per business mile for carrying a colleague on the same business journey.
testCases.expectedOutput: The handbook lists car mileage at 55p/25p; the Expenses Policy adds a passenger supplement of 5p per passenger per mile when carrying a colleague on the same business journey.
retrievalContext:
Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.1 — two-day London trip**

A Manchester-based consultant travels to London on Tuesday and returns Wednesday, with an approved overnight stay.

- Standard-class return rail: £84.00 — reimbursed in full.

- Hotel: £195.00 room only — limit £180.00; £180.00 reimbursed (the £15.00 excess is not reimbursed unless the Head of Department approves an exception, which is within the 25% threshold).

- Tuesday: lunch £14.00 and dinner £38.00 including a £6.00 glass of wine. Wine is not reimbursable, so dinner = £32.00. Tuesday meals = £46.00 (within the £55 daily cap).

- Wednesday: breakfast £13.00 (limit £12.00) and lunch £16.00 (limit £15.00). Wednesday meals = £27.00.

- Incidental allowance: £5.00.

- **Total reimbursed: £84.00 + £180.00 + £46.00 + £27.00 + £5.00 = £342.00.** Because the claim is between £250.01 and £1,000.00, it requires line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.2 — daily meal cap**

On a day of an overnight UK trip, an employee spends £12.00 on breakfast, £15.00 on lunch and £35.00 on dinner. Each item is within its individual limit, but the total of £62.00 exceeds the £55.00 daily cap, so **£55.00** is reimbursed.

## **Example 14.3 — mileage with commuting deduction**

An employee whose normal workplace is the Manchester office (12 miles from home) drives from home to a customer site in Leeds (50 miles from home) and back. Business miles = (50 − 12) x 2 = 76 miles. They have claimed fewer than 10,000 business miles this tax year. Reimbursement = 76 x £0.55 = **£41.80** .

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.6 Taxis and ride-hailing

Taxis are reimbursable up to **£50 per journey** only where: no reasonable public transport is available; the journey is between 22:00 and 06:00; the employee is carrying heavy or valuable equipment; or for personal safety or accessibility reasons. Journeys above £50 need Head of Department approval. Taxis between home and the normal workplace are not reimbursable except between 22:00 and 06:00 after work required by an incident or approved overtime.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
14 Worked claim examples

## **Example 14.4 — crossing the 10,000-mile threshold**

An employee has already claimed 9,950 business miles in the 2026/27 tax year and makes a 120-mile business journey. The first 50 miles are paid at 55p and the remaining 70 at 25p: (50 x £0.55) + (70 x £0.25) = £27.50 + £17.50 = **£45.00** .

## **Example 14.5 — Berlin trip (Band B), currency conversion**

An employee travels to Berlin for 3 nights with Director pre-approval and a travel-risk check. The hotel costs €210 per night on the corporate card; the card statement shows £181.50 per night including fees, which is within the £200 Band B limit, so £544.50 is reimbursed for 3 nights. A taxi costing €30 was paid in cash; Finance's published rate for that month is 1.16 euros per £1, so the claim is €30 / 1.16 = **£25.86** . Because the total claim exceeds £250, it needs line manager and Head of Department approval.

## **Example 14.6 — client dinner**

A dinner for 4 people (2 client attendees and 2 Northstar employees) costs £296.00 including drinks, which is £74.00 per head. This is above the £60 per head limit by 23%, so the Head of Department (who must pre-approve all client entertainment) may approve the excess as an exception up to 25% above the limit. If the bill had been £320.00 (£80.00 per head, 33% above the limit), Director approval would be required for the excess. Neither amount exceeds £100 per head, so no gifts and hospitality register entry is required.

# **Example 14.7 — late claims and reimbursement dates**

- An expense incurred on Wednesday 3 March 2027 and submitted on Thursday 15 April 2027 is 43 calendar days old: a late claim needing a written explanation and Head of Department approval.

- The same expense submitted on Saturday 5 June 2027 would be 94 calendar days old and would not be reimbursed unless the Finance Director approved an exception.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.7 Parking, tolls and charges

Parking at customer sites, stations and airports (for trips of up to 3 nights) is reimbursable at actual cost with a receipt or app record. Tolls, the London Congestion Charge and Clean Air Zone or ULEZ charges for business journeys are reimbursable where use of a car was justified. Penalty charge notices, parking fines and speeding fines are never reimbursable.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01) 4 Expense categories and limits > 4.3 Mileage (own vehicle) **Table 4.3 — Mileage rates (2026/27 tax year, 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027)** |**Vehicle**|**First 10,000 business miles in the tax**
**year**|**Each business mile over 10,000**| |---|---|---| |Car or van|55p|25p| |Motorcycle|24p|24p| |Bicycle|20p|20p| |Passenger supplement (carrying a
colleague on the same business journey)|5p per passenger per mile|5p per passenger per mile| These rates follow HMRC approved mileage allowance payment rates for 2026/27. Only business miles are claimable. Where a journey starts or ends at home, deduct the employee's normal commuting distance between home and the normal workplace from each leg. The employee must hold valid business-use insurance, a valid licence and an MOT where required; Northstar may ask to see these. For round trips over 150 miles, rail should be used unless driving is cheaper overall, necessary to carry equipment, or a reasonable adjustment. Fuel cards are not issued.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-078
testCases.input: Does Northstar enhance Shared Parental Pay?
testCases.actualOutput: No. Northstar pays Shared Parental Pay only; there is no company enhancement.
testCases.expectedOutput: Both the handbook and the Leave and Absence Standard state that Northstar pays ShPP only (£194.32 or 90% of AWE if lower) with no company enhancement, unlike maternity and adoption pay.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.4 Shared parental leave and pay

Eligible parents can share up to **50 weeks** of leave and up to **37 weeks** of pay by ending maternity or adoption leave early. Eligibility depends on both parents: the employee must meet the continuity of employment test (normally 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the 15th week before the EWC or by the week of matching, and still employed in the first week of shared parental leave), and the other parent must meet the employment and earnings test. The employee must give at least **8 weeks' written notice** of leave dates. Requests for discontinuous blocks may be refused; the employee may then take the leave as one continuous block. Northstar pays ShPP only; there is no company enhancement for shared parental pay.

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 7

## Family leave: day-one rights, conditional pay

Paternity leave
Day-one right since 6 April 2026: up to 2 weeks. Full pay for 2 weeks only if the employee qualifies for SPP (26 weeks' service by the qualifying week); otherwise unpaid.
Unpaid parental leave
Day-one right since 6 April 2026: 18 weeks per child up to age 18, maximum 4 weeks per child per year, 21 days' notice.
Enhanced maternity and adoption pay
16 weeks' full pay, then statutory pay to week 39, for employees who qualify for statutory pay and have 26 weeks' service. Shared parental pay has no enhancement.
Leave and pay are assessed separately: an employee can be entitled to the leave but not to the pay.

Speaker notes: Leave and pay eligibility are assessed separately. Employees can be entitled to leave without being entitled to statutory or enhanced pay. Carer's leave: one week per 12 months from day one, with the first 3 days paid by Northstar. Time off for dependants: Northstar pays up to 2 days per occurrence and up to 5 paid days per leave year.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.5 Unpaid parental leave

Since 6 April 2026, unpaid parental leave is a day-one right for eligible employees. Employees with parental responsibility may take up to **18 weeks** of unpaid parental leave for each child up to the child's 18th birthday, with a maximum of **4 weeks per child in any year** . Leave must be taken in whole weeks unless the child is disabled or Northstar agrees otherwise, and the employee must give **21 days' notice** of the start and end dates. Northstar may postpone leave for up to 6 months where the business would be unduly disrupted, except where leave is requested to start immediately after a birth or adoption; any postponement is confirmed in writing within 7 days of the request with the new dates. Northstar may ask for reasonable proof of parental responsibility but will not ask for it each time leave is requested.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
11 Pay, payroll, deductions and benefits > 11.11 Pension

Northstar automatically enrols eligible employees into the Northstar Group Personal Pension, in line with workplace pension auto-enrolment law. The statutory minimum total contribution is 8% of qualifying earnings (at least 3% from the employer), where qualifying earnings for 2026/27 are earnings between £6,240 and £50,270 a year. Northstar contributes **5% of basic salary** when the employee contributes at least **4% of basic salary** ; contributions can be made by salary sacrifice. Employees may opt out, but will then lose the employer contribution, and Northstar will re-enrol eligible employees periodically as the law requires.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
8 Family-related leave > 8.2 Paternity leave and pay

**Leave.** Since 6 April 2026, paternity leave is a day-one right for eligible employees. An employee who is the biological father of the child, or the partner of the mother or adopter, and who expects to have responsibility for the child's upbringing, may take up to **2 weeks** of paternity leave, as one 2-week block or two separate 1-week blocks. Leave cannot start before the birth and must end within 52 weeks of the birth (or of the due date if the baby is born early).

**Notice.** The employee must tell People Operations the due date at least 15 weeks before the baby is due, and must give 28 days' notice to change the start date of paternity leave.

**Statutory Paternity Pay.** SPP is £194.32 per week or 90% of AWE, whichever is lower. It requires at least 26 weeks' continuous service by the end of the qualifying week (the 15th week before the EWC), continued employment up to the date of birth, and AWE of at least £129.

**Northstar enhancement.** Employees who qualify for SPP receive **full basic pay for 2 weeks** , inclusive of SPP. Employees who are entitled to paternity leave but do not qualify for SPP (for example, because they joined less than 26 weeks before the qualifying week) take paternity leave unpaid; they may choose to use annual leave instead for some or all of the period.

If the employee fails to attend two meetings without good reason, the request may be treated as withdrawn, and the employee is told this in writing.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.6 Formal flexible-working requests

All employees can make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and can make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . A request can cover hours, start and finish times, working days, or place of work.

## **Flexible working — process and deadlines**

1. Submit a written request in PeopleHub stating that it is a statutory request for flexible working, the date of the request, the working pattern requested and the proposed start date, and whether and when any earlier request was made. 2. The line manager acknowledges the request within **5 working days** . 3. The line manager meets the employee to discuss the request within **4 weeks** of receiving it. A request cannot be refused without first consulting the employee. 4. A written decision is issued, and any appeal concluded, within **2 months** of the date of the request, unless the employee agrees to an extension. 5. A refusal must give one or more of the statutory business reasons and explain why it applies. 6. The employee may appeal within **10 working days** of the decision. The appeal is heard by a different, more senior manager.

The statutory business reasons for refusing a request are: the burden of additional costs; inability to reorganise work among existing staff; inability to recruit additional staff; a detrimental effect on quality; a detrimental effect on performance; a detrimental effect on ability to meet customer demand; insufficient work during the periods the employee proposes to work; and planned structural changes. Managers may agree a **trial period of up to 3 months** before confirming a permanent change.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.5 Examples

- **Approved:** A G3 engineer requests a 9-day fortnight. The team can rearrange release-day cover. Approved for a 3-month trial, then made permanent.

- **Approved with modification:** An analyst asks to work 07:00 to 15:00 every day. The team's customer calls run until 16:00 on Tuesdays, so the manager approves 07:00 to 15:00 on four days and 08:30 to 16:30 on Tuesdays, with the employee's agreement.

- **Refused:** A service-desk technician asks to work fully remotely. Device handling at the Manchester office is required on 3 days a week and cannot be reorganised among the 2 other technicians. Refused for "inability to reorganise work among existing staff", with an alternative of 2 remote days offered.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.1 Eligibility

Every employee may make a statutory flexible-working request from their first day of employment, and may make up to **2 statutory requests in any 12-month period** . Contractors and agency workers cannot use this procedure.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
5 Formal flexible-working requests > 5.4 Trials and outcomes

Managers may agree a trial of up to **3 months** , recorded with a review date. At the end of the trial, the arrangement becomes permanent, is extended once by up to 3 months, or ends with reasons given. A permanent change is a contractual variation confirmed in writing by People Operations within 14 days.

testCases.input: What equipment do hybrid employees get, and when must it be returned when they leave?
testCases.actualOutput:
Hybrid employees are provided a laptop, one external monitor, a keyboard, a mouse and a headset.
When leaving, return all equipment within 5 working days after your leaving date using the prepaid courier arranged by IT; you may post your access card with it.
testCases.expectedOutput: Hybrid and remote employees receive a laptop, one external monitor, keyboard, mouse and headset. Remote or hybrid leavers return all equipment within 5 working days after their leaving date using the prepaid courier; escalation follows at 10 working days.
retrievalContext:
Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
20 Company equipment and property > 20.6 Returning equipment

### **Equipment return deadlines**

- **Office-based leavers** return all equipment and their access card to IT on their **last working day** .

- **Remote or hybrid leavers** return all equipment within **5 working days** after their leaving date, using the prepaid courier arranged by IT. Access cards may be posted with the equipment.

- If equipment has not been returned within **10 working days** after the leaving date, IT escalates to People Operations, who send a written reminder and may take recovery action. Any deduction from final pay is made only where the contract permits or the employee has agreed in writing.

- Employees returning from long-term absence or moving role return any equipment no longer needed within 10 working days of IT's request.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.4 Home-working equipment

Northstar provides a laptop, one external monitor, a keyboard, a mouse and a headset to hybrid and remote employees. After completing probation, employees may claim a **home office allowance of up to £300** (including VAT), once in any 3-year period, for a desk, chair or other ergonomic equipment, with receipts, through ExpenseFlow. Equipment provided as a reasonable adjustment is funded separately and does not count towards the allowance.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
22 Organisation changes, redundancy, resignation and termination > 22.9 Equipment return and access revocation

Equipment is returned in line with section 20.6. System and building access is revoked at **17:30 on the last working day** , or immediately on dismissal without notice or at the start of garden leave.

Northstar may change a team's hybrid pattern or anchor days for genuine business reasons by giving at least **4 weeks' notice** , or less in an emergency. A contractual flexible-working arrangement can be changed only by agreement, by a further statutory request, or through a proper consultation process. testCases.actualOutput:
- 27 days’ annual leave for full-time staff, plus 8 bank holidays.

testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-120
testCases.input: The induction deck says someone starting full-time on 1 March 2027 can book 9 days by 1 June. Does the Leave and Absence Standard agree?
testCases.actualOutput: Yes. For 1 June 2027, the Standard says accrued leave is 6.75 days, rounded up to 7; with line manager approval, up to 9 days can be booked. More than 5 consecutive working days also requires Head of Department approval.
testCases.expectedOutput: Both agree. The Leave and Absence Standard section 3.2 gives the same worked example: 3 complete months by 1 June, accrued 6.75 days rounded up to 7.0, plus up to 2 additional days with line manager approval = 9.0 days. Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days in probation also needs Head of Department approval. The Standard is authoritative; the deck is a summary.
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.2 Accrual and booking

Leave accrues at one-twelfth of the annual entitlement per complete calendar month. After probation, the full annual entitlement may be booked in advance. During probation, the bookable amount is accrued leave (rounded up to the nearest 0.5 day) plus up to 2 additional days with line manager approval.

### **Booking during probation**

A full-time employee starts on 1 March 2027. On 1 June 2027 they have 3 complete months of service. Accrued leave = 27 x 3 / 12 = 6.75 days, rounded up to 7.0 days. With line manager approval they may book up to 7.0 + 2 = **9.0 days** for leave starting on or around that date. Any period of more than 5 consecutive working days also needs Head of Department approval.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year)

- **Request submitted Thursday 1 October 2026** for 3 days starting Monday 12 October 2026. Working days between: 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 October = 6. The current rule (10 working days) applies, so this is **short notice** .

- **Part-time 2026 entitlement (3 days per week, 0.6 FTE, less than 5 years' service):** archived allowance 15 days (112.5 hours) plus bank holidays on working days, plus a transitional uplift of 3.75 x 0.6 = **2.25 hours** , giving 114.75 hours of annual leave.

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.9 Transitional arrangements (2026 leave year) **Table 3.9 — Transitional rules from the archived Leave Policy NDS-HR-LV-006 v1.0** |**Topic**|**Archived policy v1.0 (1 Jan 2025 – 30 Sep**
**2026)**|**This Standard v1.2 (from 1 Oct 2026)**| |---|---|---| |Full-time annual leave|25 days plus bank holidays|27 days plus bank holidays (2027
onwards)| |2026 full-time entitlement|—|25.5 days (less than 5 years' service); 26.5
days (5 years or more)| |Service increments|+1 day after 5 years|+1 day after 3 years; +2 days after 5 years
(from 1 January 2027)| |Notice for up to 5 days|5 working days|2 working days (up to 1 day); 10 working
days (more than 1 and up to 5 days)| |Notice for more than 5 days|20 working days|20 working days (up to 10 days); 40
working days (more than 10 days)| |Manager response time|10 working days|5 working days| |Carryover|3 days, use by 28 February|5 days, use by 31 March| |Hourly leave|Not available|Available from 1 October 2026| |Negative balance|Not permitted|Up to 3 days with Head of Department
approval| |Sickness reporting deadline|10:00|09:30| **Which rules apply to a request?** The notice and approval rules are those in force on the date the request was submitted. Entitlement and carryover are determined by the leave year. ### **Worked examples 3.9 — transition** - **Request submitted Monday 28 September 2026** for 3 days starting Tuesday 6 October 2026. Working days between: 29 and 30 September, 1, 2 and 5 October = 5. The request was submitted before 1 October 2026, so the archived rule (5 working days for up to 5 days) applies and the notice requirement is **met** .

Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01) 3 Annual leave > 3.1 Entitlement **Table 3.1 — Annual leave entitlement (full-time, 37.5 hours over 5 days)** |**Continuous service completed**|**Annual leave**
**days**|**Bank holidays**|**Total days**|**Total hours**| |---|---|---|---|---| |Less than 3 years|27|8|35|262.5| |3 years or more, less than 5 years|28|8|36|270.0| |5 years or more|29|8|37|277.5| Service increments apply from the first 1 January that falls after the employee completes the required service. ### **Service increment timing** - Start date 15 March 2024: 3 years completed on 14 March 2027. 1 Introduction and document governance > 1.5 Policy hierarchy and conflict resolution

If two sources appear to conflict, apply the following order of precedence, subject always to mandatory law:

1. Applicable mandatory law.

2. The employee's applicable employment contract or written contractual variation.

3. The current, topic-specific approved policy or standard (for example, the Leave and Absence Standard NDS-HR-LAS-002).

4. This current Employee Handbook summary.

5. Non-binding manager guidance.

A superseded or archived document never takes precedence over a current document. Archived documents are retained only to show what applied during their effective period. testCases.input: I'm a new starter still in probation. Can I claim the £300 home office allowance and work from Spain for a week?
testCases.actualOutput: No. You must complete probation before claiming the allowance; afterwards, it is up to £300 once in any 3-year period for eligible hybrid or remote employees, with receipts. You’re also not eligible to work from Spain during probation. After probation, a week abroad requires a request at least 4 weeks ahead and approval from your line manager, People Operations and IT Security.
testCases.expectedOutput: The home office allowance (up to £300 once every 3 years) is available only after completing probation. Work From Abroad requires completed probation and not serving notice; afterwards it is limited to 10 working days in a rolling 12 months, requested 4 weeks ahead and approved by the line manager, People Operations and IT Security.
retrievalContext:

Slide 7

## Expenses and your home set-up

Claiming expenses
Claim in ExpenseFlow within 30 calendar days with an itemised receipt. Get approval before overnight stays, any international travel, single items over £250 and client entertainment. Approved claims by the 10th are paid with your salary on the 25th.
Working from home
You get a laptop, one monitor, keyboard, mouse and headset. Once you pass probation you can claim up to £300 once every 3 years for a desk or chair. Broadband isn't reimbursed. Complete the DSE self-assessment within 2 weeks.
Working from abroad isn't available during probation. After that it's limited to 10 working days in a rolling 12 months.

Speaker notes: Work From Abroad is not available during probation. After probation it is limited to 10 working days in a rolling 12 months with approval from the line manager, People Operations and IT Security.

Expenses and Business Travel Policy (NDS-FIN-EXP-003 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Expense categories and limits > 4.10 Home office, professional subscriptions and learning

- **Home office allowance:** up to £300 (including VAT) once in any 3-year period, for employees who have completed probation and work hybrid or remotely; receipts required. Broadband, utilities and personal mobile contracts are not reimbursable.

- **Professional subscriptions:** one role-relevant membership per year, up to £250, pre-approved by the line manager.

- **Learning:** courses, conferences and exams are paid from the £1,000 annual learning budget (handbook section 13.6), ideally booked directly by the Travel desk or Learning team rather than claimed.

Hybrid and Flexible Working Standard (NDS-HR-HFW-005 v1.1, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Working from outside the UK > 7.3 Worked examples

## **Work From Abroad examples**

- **Within the limit:** An employee who has not worked abroad in the past 12 months requests to work from Portugal for 5 working days in July 2027, submitting the request 6 weeks ahead. Approvable, subject to all three approvals.

- **Rolling limit exceeded:** An employee worked abroad for 6 days in February 2027 and asks for 5 days in October 2027. Within the rolling 12 months this would total 11 days, so only **4 days** can be approved unless the Director of People Operations approves an exception (maximum 20 days).

- **Restricted customer data:** An employee who supports a customer's payroll platform (Restricted data) asks to work from Italy for a week. They may work abroad only on tasks that do not involve Restricted data, unless the CISO approves in writing and the customer contract permits access from outside the UK. The manager arranges UK-based cover for Restricted tasks.

- **Short notice:** A request submitted 10 days before travel does not meet the 4-week notice requirement and will normally be declined.

- **Probation:** An employee in month 4 of probation asks to work from Spain for 3 days. Not eligible until probation is completed.

- **Holiday email:** An employee on annual leave in France briefly reads email on their phone. This is not a working day abroad. Joining a customer call or accessing customer systems would be, and requires approval.

NDS-FIN-EXP-003 and does not count towards the 10 days.|

10 Hybrid, remote and flexible working > 10.4 Home-working equipment

Northstar provides a laptop, one external monitor, a keyboard, a mouse and a headset to hybrid and remote employees. After completing probation, employees may claim a **home office allowance of up to £300** (including VAT), once in any 3-year period, for a desk, chair or other ergonomic equipment, with receipts, through ExpenseFlow. testCases.name: NDS-EVAL-125
testCases.input: Per the manager briefing, how much company sick pay does an employee with 3 years' service get?
testCases.actualOutput: They get 8 weeks at full pay, followed by 8 weeks at half pay, in any rolling 12-month period. The policy governs because it prevails over the manager briefing.
testCases.expectedOutput: Employees with 2 to under 5 years' service get 8 weeks at full pay followed by 8 weeks at half pay in any rolling 12-month period, inclusive of SSP (briefing chart and notes; handbook Table 7.5 is authoritative).
retrievalContext:
Leave and Absence Standard (NDS-HR-LAS-002 v1.2, current, effective 2026-10-01)
4 Sickness absence > 4.4 Company sick pay

**Table 4.4 — Company sick pay (inclusive of SSP) in any rolling 12 months**

|**Continuous service on first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed, less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more, less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

## **Worked examples 4.4 — sick pay**

- **Probation:** a full-time employee in probation (normal weekly earnings above £154.07, so the £123.25 rate applies) is absent for 4 working days. Daily SSP = £123.25 / 5 = £24.65. SSP payable = 4 x £24.65 = **£98.60** . No company sick pay is due.

- **3 years' service:** an employee who has already received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months is absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay weeks = 8 − 5 = 3. They receive 3 weeks at full pay and 3 weeks at half pay.

- **6 years' service, salary £52,000, no previous sick pay in 12 months, absent 15 weeks:** 13 weeks at full pay (£1,000 per week) and 2 weeks at half pay (£500 per week, which is more than SSP). Pay for weeks 14 and 15 = 2 x £500 = **£1,000** .

Company sick pay may be withheld for days where the reporting or evidence rules were not followed without good reason; SSP remains payable where the statutory conditions are met.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.5 Company sick pay

Company sick pay is a contractual enhancement for employees whose contract incorporates the company sick pay scheme (all permanent and fixed-term employment contracts issued from 1 January 2025). It is paid **inclusive of SSP** : SSP forms part of, and is not paid in addition to, company sick pay.

**Table 7.5 — Company sick pay entitlement in any rolling 12-month period**

|**Continuous service on the first day of absence**|**Full pay**|**Then half pay**|
|---|---|---|
|During probation|SSP only|SSP only|
|Probation completed and less than 2 years|4 weeks|4 weeks|
|2 years or more but less than 5 years|8 weeks|8 weeks|
|5 years or more|13 weeks|13 weeks|

- The rolling 12-month period is the 12 months ending on the day before the first day of the current absence. Company sick pay already paid in that period is deducted from the entitlement.

- "Half pay" is half of basic pay; where half pay would be less than SSP, SSP is paid instead. After company sick pay is exhausted, SSP continues if the statutory conditions are met.

- Weeks are calculated by reference to the employee's normal working days (for example, one week for a 3-day-per-week employee is 3 working days).

- Company sick pay is conditional on following the reporting procedure in section 7.1 and providing the evidence in section 7.3. If the employee does not follow these steps without a good reason, company sick pay may be withheld for the affected days. Statutory Sick Pay is still paid where the statutory conditions are met.

- Contractors and agency workers are not eligible for company sick pay.

**Example.** An employee with 3 years' continuous service has received 5 weeks of full company sick pay in the previous 12 months. They are now absent for 6 weeks. Remaining full-pay entitlement = 8 − 5 = 3 weeks. They

therefore receive 3 weeks at full pay followed by 3 weeks at half pay (they have 8 weeks of half-pay entitlement available).

What changes on 1 October 2026: Manager Briefing (NDS-HR-PRES-011 v1.0, summary deck, current, effective 2026-10-01)
Slide 6

## Sickness: call by 09:30, SSP from day one

Employees call (phone or Teams) by 09:30 on day one; messages alone are not enough
Self-certify up to 7 calendar days; fit note after that
Since 6 April 2026, SSP is paid from the first day: £123.25 a week or 80% of earnings, whichever is lower
Company sick pay is inclusive of SSP and starts after probation
Pregnancy-related absence never counts towards triggers

Speaker notes: Company sick pay in any rolling 12 months: during probation SSP only; probation completed and under 2 years, 4 weeks full pay then 4 weeks half pay; 2 to under 5 years, 8 weeks full then 8 weeks half; 5 years or more, 13 weeks full then 13 weeks half. Attendance triggers: 3 separate absences or 8 working days in a rolling 12 months starts a supportive Stage 0 review. Disability-related absence is recorded separately and triggers may be adjusted.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
7 Sickness absence and medical appointments > 7.4 Statutory Sick Pay (SSP)

## **Statutory Sick Pay from 6 April 2026**

Following the Employment Rights Act 2025, from 6 April 2026 SSP is payable from the first day of sickness absence (the former 3 unpaid "waiting days" were removed) and the lower earnings limit no longer applies to eligibility. The weekly rate is £123.25 or 80% of the employee's normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower, for up to 28 weeks. Northstar's qualifying days for SSP are the employee's contracted working days. SSP rates are set by government and usually change each April.

Employee Handbook (NDS-HR-HB-001 v2.0, current, effective 2026-10-01)
9 Other forms of leave > 9.7 Sabbaticals and career breaks

Employees who will have at least **5 years' continuous service** on the proposed start date may apply for an unpaid sabbatical of **1 to 3 months** , no more than once in any 5-year period. Applications must be made at least **3 months** before the proposed start and approved by a Director. Approval is discretionary and depends on business needs. During a sabbatical, employment continues, but salary, pension contributions and annual leave accrual are suspended for the unpaid period; life assurance and private medical insurance continue.
